title: [Bug] Background controller creates duplicate generate URs and fat RuleContext URs
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

We are hitting two related operational problems in v1.16 around UpdateRequest (UR) management:

  1. Each background scan creates a new generate UR for the same policy, even when a prior UR is still Pending/processing — causing UR sprawl.
  2. Generate URs accumulate hundreds or thousands of triggers in a single Spec.RuleContext, and if any one trigger fails, the entire UR is marked Failed, reset to Pending, and reprocessed in full — starving the background-controller workqueue.

These are still happening after a v1.18.0 update.

#### 1. Generate URs are not deduplicated per policy

  The mutateExisting path already deduplicates URs per `(policy, trigger)` before creating a new UR:

  ```go
  // pkg/policy/mutate.go:39
  murs := pc.listMutateURs(policyKey, trigger)
  if murs != nil {
      logger.V(4).Info("UR was created", ...)
      continue
  }
  ```

  The generate path does not have an equivalent check. `handleGenerateForExisting` / `syncDataPolicyChanges` (`pkg/policy/generate.go:23-148`) always calls `pc.urGenerator.Generate(...)`, which is just `UpdateRequests().Create(...)` with only a global count threshold guard:

  ```go
  // pkg/utils/generator/updaterequests.go:30-53
  count := len(objects.Items)
  threshold := g.config.GetUpdateRequestThreshold()
  if int64(count) >= threshold {
      log.Error(... "UpdateRequest creation skipped" ...)
      return nil, nil
  }
  created, err := client.KyvernoV2().UpdateRequests(...).Create(ctx, resource, metav1.CreateOptions{})
  ```

  `GenerateLabelsSet` (`pkg/background/common/labels.go:54`) only carries the policy name, so even a future dedup based on labels could not be per-trigger without a label-set change.

  As a result, every `forceReconciliation` tick (and every policy update event) creates a fresh generate UR per policy regardless of whether the previous one for the same policy is still pending.

  #### 2. One UR accumulates all matching triggers in `RuleContext`

  `handleGenerateForExisting` builds a single UR per policy and appends every matched trigger to `Spec.RuleContext`:

  ```go
  // pkg/policy/generate.go:89-124
  ur := newGenerateUR(engineapi.NewKyvernoPolicy(policy))
  for _, rule := range policy.GetSpec().Rules {
      ...
      triggers := getTriggers(...)
      for _, trigger := range triggers {
          ...
          addRuleContext(ur, rule.Name, common.ResourceSpecFromUnstructured(*trigger), false, false)
      }
  }
  ```

  If a `generateExisting` rule matches e.g. all Namespaces in a large cluster, one UR ends up with thousands of `RuleContext` entries.

  #### 3. Per-trigger failures still poison the whole UR (queue starvation)

  `ProcessUR` iterates each trigger and collects errors instead of breaking, which is good — but then the entire UR is marked `Failed` if any trigger failed:

  ```go
  // pkg/background/generate/controller.go:103-134
  for i := 0; i < len(ur.Spec.RuleContext); i++ {
      ...
      genResources, err = c.applyGenerate(*trigger, *ur, policy, i)
      if err != nil { failures = append(failures, ...); continue }
  }
  return updateStatus(c.statusControl, *ur, multierr.Combine(failures...), genResources)
  ```

  `reconcileURStatus` then flips `Failed` → `Pending`:

  ```go
  // pkg/background/update_request_controller.go:285-287
  case kyvernov2.Failed:
      new.Status.State = kyvernov2.Pending
      _, errUpdate = c.kyvernoClient.KyvernoV2().UpdateRequests(...).UpdateStatus(...)
  ```

  The informer event handler enqueues without rate limiting:

  ```go
  // pkg/background/update_request_controller.go:241-247
  func (c *controller) updateUR(_, cur interface{}) {
      curUr := cur.(*kyvernov2.UpdateRequest)
      if curUr.Status.State == kyvernov2.Skip || curUr.Status.State == kyvernov2.Completed {
          return
      }
      c.enqueueUpdateRequest(curUr)
  }
  ```

So one bad trigger inside a 1000-trigger UR causes the controller to repeatedly reprocess all 1000 triggers in a tight loop. With `genWorkers` defaulting to 10, a small number of poisoned fat URs can fully starve the background-controller queue. `0e2561777` (which correctly started surfacing `applyGenerate` errors instead of silently marking Success) makes this behavior more observable in v1.18 than in early v1.16 builds.

  ### Expected behavior

  - Generate URs should be deduplicated per `(policy, trigger)`, analogous to the existing mutateExisting path (`pkg/policy/mutate.go:39`).
  - Either fan generate-existing out to one UR per trigger, or split a fat `RuleContext` into batches, so a single bad trigger cannot block successful ones.
  - A `Failed` UR should not be reprocessed without backoff and without isolating the failing triggers from the already-succeeded ones (e.g. requeue only the failing subset, or mark the trigger as failed within the UR status and not retry it tight-loop).

Mutate

  As a side effect, this can have a significant negative impact on Admission Review Latency (in my case, up to 1.5 seconds).

This performance issue can be very hard to identify. It would be great if this kind of error could at least be reported in the Policy status, and ideally if the policycachecould handle Kinds ending in s.

```
          names:
          - super-secret.*
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              application: confidential
```


### Steps to reproduce

Create few polices as in the previous example and 20 / 100 secret that match the policy.

title: [Bug] Creating a NamespacedMutatingPolicy and MutatingPolicy without matching condition causes webhook name to be duplicated
body:

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

Other (specify in description)

### Kyverno Rule Type

Mutate

### Description

This is a RKE2 cluster.

We first created a `NamespacedMutatingPolicy`:
```
> kubectl get namespacedmutatingpolicy -A
NAMESPACE         NAME                                               AGE   READY
longhorn-system   longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection   14d
```

This generates a valid MutatingWebhookConfiguration (I'll omit some generated bits for brevity):
```yaml

    webhook.kyverno.io/managed-by: kyverno
  name: kyverno-resource-mutating-webhook-cfg
webhooks:
- admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: OMMITED
    service:
      name: kyverno-svc
      namespace: kyverno
      path: /nmpol/longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
      port: 443
  failurePolicy: Fail
  matchPolicy: Equivalent
  name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail
  namespaceSelector:
    matchExpressions:
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kube-system
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:

  objectSelector:
    matchLabels:
      longhorn.io/component: instance-manager
      longhorn.io/managed-by: longhorn-manager
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  rules:
  - apiGroups:
    - ""
    apiVersions:
    - v1
    operations:
    - CREATE
    resources:
    - pods
    scope: '*'
  sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
  timeoutSeconds: 10
```

Note the name: `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail`.

Then, we try to create a cluster-wide `MutatingPolicy`:
```
> kubectl get mutatingpolicy
NAME             AGE   READY
proxy-registry   39m   true
```

Despite that `true` in the READY column, the admission controllers error nonstop (see logs bellow) and the policy is not applied.

It seems that the controller ignores the name of the policy and namespace when updating the mutating webhook, and simply tries to create a new one with the same name.

We have a separate cluster where we applied only the `proxy-registry` `MutatingPolicy`, and that webhook looks like this:
```yaml
webhooks:
- admissionReviewVersions:
  - v1
  clientConfig:
    caBundle: OMMITED FOR BREVITY
    service:
      name: kyverno-svc
      namespace: kyverno
      path: /mpol/proxy-registry
      port: 443

      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kube-system
    - key: kubernetes.io/metadata.name
      operator: NotIn
      values:
      - kyverno
  objectSelector: {}
  reinvocationPolicy: Never
  rules:
    - OMMITED FOR BREVITY
  sideEffects: NoneOnDryRun
  timeoutSeconds: 10
```

Note, once again, the name `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail`.

Issue https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15445 seems similar, but maybe that was only namespaced policies? I don't see the global mutating policies applying name prefixes or suffixes.

I also noticed that when recreating the `NamespacedMutatingPolicy`, we get an error on the logs (also see bellow), but it "seems" to work.

~~I'm also failing at replicating this on a Minikube cluster and fresh install. I'll note that the first policy (the namespaced one) was applied when Kyverno was in version 1.17.1, then it was upgraded to 1.18.0 for the cluster-wide policy. We then downgraded to 1.17.2, thinking it was a regression, but no dice.~~

I was able to replicate the problem specifically with this policy. It generates a policy with the `mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail` name, no namespace and name suffix:
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: NamespacedMutatingPolicy
metadata:
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Reliability
    policies.kyverno.io/description: Injects the label nethermind.io/termination-protection="true"
      onto any Pod bearing the Longhorn instance-manager labels, at creation time
      only. Used in conjunction with the Termination Protection validating policy
      in this namespace
    policies.kyverno.io/severity: high
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Longhorn Instance Manager Termination Protection
  name: longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
  namespace: longhorn-system
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    objectSelector:
      matchLabels:
        longhorn.io/component: instance-manager
        longhorn.io/managed-by: longhorn-manager
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:
      - ""
      apiVersions:
      - v1
      operations:
      - CREATE
      resources:
      - pods
  mutations:
  - applyConfiguration:
      expression: |-
        Object{
          metadata: Object.metadata{
            labels: {"termination-protection": "true"}
          }
        }
    patchType: ApplyConfiguration
```

Then I added this snippet
```yaml
  matchConditions:
  - name: always-true
    expression: "true"
```

And suddenly...
```yaml
name: mpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail-finegrained-longhorn-system-longhorn-instance-manager-termination-protection
```

So it seems the issue seems to be that the controller tries to group up both namespaced and non namespaced policies in the same webhook, with the same name.

### Steps to reproduce

2. Create a `MutatingPolicy` with no matching conditions
3. The controller should fail at patching the MutatingWebhookConfiguration
4. Add a matching condition to the policies
5. The correct name is created, controller patches successfully

### Expected behavior

The controller should successfully handle both policies existing at the same time

title: GeneratingPolicy with generateExisting panics background controller when matchConstraints targets a resource the SA cannot list
body:
# [Bug] GeneratingPolicy with `generateExisting` panics background controller when `matchConstraints` targets a resource the SA cannot list

## Kyverno Version

1.17.0 , 1.18.0 and older versions

## Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

## Kubernetes Platform

EKS

## Kyverno Rule Type

Generate

---

## Description

When a `GeneratingPolicy` (`policies.kyverno.io/v1`) has `spec.evaluation.generateExisting.enabled: true` and `matchConstraints.resourceRules` targets `customresourcedefinitions`, the background controller calls `ListResource` on CRDs cluster-wide. However, the `kyverno-background-controller` ServiceAccount only has `get` on CRDs — not `list` or `watch` — so the API server returns `403 Forbidden`.

The upstream bug is in `pkg/policy/gpol.go:103–107`: the error branch logs but is missing a `continue` statement, so execution falls through and immediately dereferences the nil result, causing:

```
runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

Both background controller replicas enter `CrashLoopBackOff`, which causes significant disruption as the background controller is responsible for processing all generate rules.

**Notes on scope:**

- The bug only fires with `generateExisting: true`. Without it, applying the policy doesn't crash the controller.
- The bug fires even when no matching CRD exists in the cluster. `ListResource` is called before any `matchConditions` are evaluated, so the cluster-wide list itself is what fails.
- A `403 Forbidden` from the API server is something controllers encounter regularly (RBAC narrowed, CRD removed mid-reconcile, etc.). It should not cause a panic.
- The default Kyverno chart grants only `get` on CRDs to the background controller, so a `GeneratingPolicy` triggering on CRDs crashes the controller out of the box.

> Related: #15722 — a separate `generateExisting` issue (UR race condition causing generated resources to be deleted immediately after creation). Same surface area, different code path; the fixes are independent.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

Install Kyverno via the official Helm chart 3.7.x (Kyverno 1.18.0) with default RBAC, then apply:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: repro-gpol-panic
spec:
  evaluation:
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["apiextensions.k8s.io"]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["customresourcedefinitions"]
  matchConditions:
    - name: never-matches
      expression: "object.metadata.name == 'crd-that-does-not-exist'"
  generate:
    - expression: |-
        generator.Apply("", [
          {
            "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
            "kind": dyn("ConfigMap"),
            "metadata": dyn({
              "name": dyn("would-be-generated"),
              "namespace": dyn("default")
            })
          }
        ])
```

The cluster does not need to have any matching CRD — the `LIST` fails before any matching happens. `matchConditions` is set to a name that doesn't exist so the policy stays harmless if the bug is fixed.

Within ~60 seconds the background controller starts crashlooping. Confirm via:

```bash
kubectl logs -n kyverno \
  -l app.kubernetes.io/component=background-controller \
  --previous --tail=200
```

The stack trace points at `pkg/policy/gpol.go:107`.

---

## Expected Behavior

`getGpolTriggers` should skip the failing GVR and continue with the rest of the trigger rules. Optionally, emit a `PolicyError` event so the missing RBAC is visible to operators.

---

## Suggested Fix

Add `continue` after the error log:

```go
resources, err := pc.client.ListResource(context.TODO(), groupVersion.String(), gvk.Kind, "", objectSelector)
if err != nil {
    pc.log.Error(err, "failed to list resources", "groupVersion", groupVersion, "kind", gvk.Kind)
+   continue
}
for i, res := range resources.Items {
```

The same pattern is already used for the `restMapper.KindFor` error branch a few lines up.

Additionally, the default Helm chart RBAC for `kyverno-background-controller` should be updated to include `list` and `watch` on `customresourcedefinitions`, since triggering on CRDs is a common use case.

---

## Kyverno Logs

```
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:105 > failed to list resources
  error="customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io is forbidden:
  User \"system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-background-controller\"
  cannot list resource \"customresourcedefinitions\" in API group
  \"apiextensions.k8s.io\" at the cluster scope"
  groupVersion=apiextensions.k8s.io/v1 kind=CustomResourceDefinition
  logger=PolicyController

panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [recovered, repanicked]
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x8 pc=0x3dcaa13]

goroutine 396 [running]:
...
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).getGpolTriggers(0xc000cd5800, 0xc000583220)
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:107 +0x513
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).handleGenerateExisting(0xc000cd5800, 0xc00004bd40)
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/gpol.go:63 +0x10c
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy.(*policyController).syncPolicy(0xc000cd5800, {0xc008cb4990, 0x24})
        github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/policy/policy_controller.go:441 +0x865
```

---

## Workaround

Grant `list` and `watch` on `customresourcedefinitions` to the `kyverno-background-controller` ServiceAccount via an additive `ClusterRole`:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
rules:
  - apiGroups: ["apiextensions.k8s.io"]
    resources:
      - customresourcedefinitions
    verbs:
      - list
      - watch
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: kyverno:background-controller:additional-permissions
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kyverno-background-controller
    namespace: kyverno
```

This unblocks the CRD trigger case but must be repeated per resource type for any other non-listable resource. The two-line code fix above is the real resolution.

---

## Slack Discussion

_No response_

---

## Troubleshooting

- [x] I have read and followed the documentation AND the [[troubleshooting guide](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/)](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/).
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

title: [Bug] background scan and TTL controllers can silently stop reconciling resources after a transient error
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

i was reading through the cleanup/deleting controller fix in #15972 and noticed the same shape exists in two other controllers on main. wanted to flag it.


in `pkg/controllers/report/background/controller.go`, the `reconcile()` function (around line 757) re-arms itself via `c.queue.AddAfter(key, c.forceDelay)` as a defer inside the else branch of the final `if err != nil` block (around line 912). before that line, there are ~17 early-return paths (one per lister fetch: vpol, namespaced vpol, mpol, namespaced mpol, ivpol, namespaced ivpol, VAP, MAP, MAP-alpha, bindings, exceptions, CEL exceptions, etc) that just `return err` directly. each of those skips the defer, so `AddAfter` never fires.

once the workqueue retries 10 times, the standard `handleErr` in `pkg/utils/controller/run.go` calls `Forget()` and the key is dropped. the only rescue paths are:

- policy/exception/CRD churn (informer event re-enqueues via `enqueueResources`)
- the resource itself being mutated (metadata cache event)

in a steady-state cluster (stable policies, stable workloads) neither of those fires, so the resource UID's `PolicyReport` just stays frozen at its last value until the reports controller pod restarts.

trigger is anything transient: API server throttle, brief lister desync, network blip during one of the ~17 list calls. no panic, no error metric, no log line that obviously says "i stopped firing for this UID."

`pkg/controllers/ttl/controller.go` has the same shape. early returns at the lister fetch, accessor, and Delete paths (around lines 116, 129, 134, 162) skip the `AddAfter` on line 172. only rescue is an informer event on that specific resource. if a resource hits a transient error during its TTL-driven Delete, it can silently survive past its TTL until the controller pod restarts.

### why this matters

- background scan: `PolicyReport` / `ClusterPolicyReport` entries can go stale without warning. for anyone using those reports for compliance dashboards, that's silently inaccurate data
- TTL: resources that should have been deleted stay alive. for retention policies (PII cleanup, ephemeral resource cleanup) that means failed cleanup with no signal

### not affected

- admission path is fine, webhook decisions still fire correctly
- cleanup + deleting controllers have the same shape but are already being fixed in #15972

### reproduction sketch

i don't have a deterministic repro because triggering the right transient lister error is timing-dependent, but the code path is straightforward to read: any of the 17 `return err` lines in `reconcile()` (background) or the early returns in `ttl/controller.go::reconcile` bypass the rearm.

### suggested fix

same shape as #15972: lift the defer `AddAfter` to the top of reconcile, capture errors in an `execErr` local, always reach the rearm, return `execErr` so the workqueue still rate-limits and the error metric still increments.

### Slack discussion

NA

title: Bug: Context leak in dynamic resource watcher
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.16.4



## Describe the bug

While reviewing the report controllers, I noticed a context propagation issue in the `resource-report-controller`. 

In `pkg/controllers/report/resource/controller.go`, the `startWatcher` function correctly accepts a `ctx context.Context` parameter to manage the lifecycle of the dynamic watchers. However, the function ignores this `ctx` when actually spinning up the underlying Kubernetes watch connections and the `RetryWatcher`. 

Instead, it hardcodes `context.Background()` and `context.TODO()`:

```go
func (c *controller) startWatcher(ctx context.Context, logger logr.Logger, gvr schema.GroupVersionResource, gvk schema.GroupVersionKind, errChan chan schema.GroupVersionResource) (*watcher, error) {
    // ...
	watchFunc := func(options metav1.ListOptions) (watch.Interface, error) {
		logger.V(3).Info("creating watcher...")
        // Hardcoded context.Background()
		watch, err := c.client.GetDynamicInterface().Resource(gvr).Watch(context.Background(), options) 
		// ...
	}
    // Hardcoded context.TODO()
	watchInterface, err := watchTools.NewRetryWatcherWithContext(context.TODO(), resourceVersion, &cache.ListWatch{WatchFunc: watchFunc})
    // ...
}
```
Because the context tree is broken, if the controller context times out or gets cancelled gracefully, the RetryWatcher and the active API server watch connections will not receive the ctx.Done() signal. Although there is a manual .Stop() call elsewhere in the cleanup logic, ignoring the parent context can still lead to hanging connections or leaked goroutines during edge cases or shutdown events.

## Steps to reproduce
This is a static code issue located in pkg/controllers/report/resource/controller.go inside startWatcher.

## Expected behavior
The RetryWatcher and the Watch() call should use the parent ctx passed into the function to ensure proper Go context cancellation and resource cleanup.

## Proposed Fix
Replace the hardcoded contexts with the provided ctx argument:

1. Update watchFunc to use Watch(ctx, options) instead of context.Background().
2. Update the NewRetryWatcherWithContext call to use ctx instead of context.TODO().

1.17.2

## Metadata
- **Kyverno Version:** 1.17.2 (also confirmed on 1.18.0)
- **Kubernetes Version:** 1.35.x (kind), 1.30.x (AKS)
- **Kubernetes Platform:** KinD (reproduction), AKS (originally observed)
- **Kyverno Rule Type:** Generate

## Description

When a `GeneratingPolicy` with `synchronize: true` and `generateExisting: true` is deployed to a cluster with many namespaces (~50+), the background controller's dynamic watcher for the generated resource type (e.g., `v1/configmaps`) permanently dies. After this occurs:

- **Source-change propagation stops entirely.** Updating the source ConfigMap never reaches existing clones.
- **New namespace creation still works** (admission-time generation is unaffected).
- **The failure is permanent** — the watcher is never recreated, even across background controller restarts, because each restart re-processes all existing namespaces and re-triggers the same failure.

We observed this on an AKS cluster with ~90 namespaces, and have a minimal reproduction on a kind cluster with 50 namespaces.

## Steps to reproduce

A self-contained reproduction script is detailed below. It requires `kind`, `helm`, `kubectl`, and `python3`.

```bash
./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh       # defaults: 50 namespaces, chart 3.7.2 (kyverno v.1.17.2)
./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.8.0  # test against v1.18.0
```

**Summary of what the script does:**

1. Creates a kind cluster and installs Kyverno with chart version 3.7.2
2. Grants the background controller RBAC for ConfigMap CRUD (required for GeneratingPolicy to function — not included in default Helm chart RBAC)
3. Creates a source namespace with a ConfigMap
4. Applies a GeneratingPolicy with `synchronize: true` and `generateExisting: true`
5. Creates 50 namespaces (triggers `generateExisting` processing)
6. Waits up to 120s for clone generation — **only ~43/50 clones are created**
7. Verifies source-change sync works for a clone that was created — **PASS**
8. Restarts the background controller (triggers reprocessing of all namespaces)
9. Verifies source-change sync after restart — **FAIL** (120s timeout, clone never updated)

<details>
<summary>Full reproduction script (kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Reproduction script for Kyverno GeneratingPolicy synchronize bug
# Affects: v1.17.2 (chart 3.7.2), v1.17.1 (chart 3.7.1), v1.18.0 (chart 3.8.0)
#
# Prerequisites: kind, helm, kubectl, python3
#
# Usage:
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh [NS_COUNT] [CHART_VERSION]
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.7.2    # default
#   ./kyverno-sync-bug-repro.sh 50 3.8.0    # test v1.18.0
#
# Expected result: "RESULT: Sync FAILED after restart — bug REPRODUCED"

CLUSTER_NAME="kyverno-sync-repro"
NS_COUNT="${1:-50}"
KYVERNO_VERSION="${2:-3.7.2}"

cleanup() {
  echo ""
  echo "=== Cleaning up ==="
  kind delete cluster --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "=== Environment ==="
echo "  kind: $(kind version)"
echo "  helm: $(helm version --short 2>/dev/null)"
echo "  kubectl: $(kubectl version --client -o json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["clientVersion"]["gitVersion"])' 2>/dev/null || kubectl version --client --short 2>/dev/null)"
echo "  Kyverno chart: $KYVERNO_VERSION"
echo "  NS_COUNT: $NS_COUNT"
echo ""

echo "=== Step 1: Create kind cluster ==="
kind create cluster --name "$CLUSTER_NAME"
CTX="kind-${CLUSTER_NAME}"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 2: Install Kyverno $KYVERNO_VERSION ==="
helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/ --force-update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace \
  --kube-context "$CTX" \
  --version "$KYVERNO_VERSION" \
  --set admissionController.replicas=1 \
  --set backgroundController.resources.limits.memory=512Mi \
  --wait --timeout 120s

echo ""
echo "=== Step 3: Grant background controller generate RBAC ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" apply -f - <<'RBAC'
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRole
metadata:
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets", "configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch", "create", "update", "patch", "delete"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: kyverno-generate-repro
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: kyverno-background-controller
    namespace: kyverno
RBAC

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4: Create source namespace and ConfigMap ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" create ns source-ns
kubectl --context "$CTX" create configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --from-literal=key1=original --from-literal=key2=value2

echo ""
echo "=== Step 4b: Wait for Kyverno webhooks to be ready ==="
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if kubectl --context "$CTX" get --raw /readyz 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok; then
    if kubectl --context "$CTX" get endpoints kyverno-svc -n kyverno \
         -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
      echo "Kyverno webhook endpoint ready (iteration $i)"
      break
    fi
  fi
  echo "  Waiting for webhook... ($i/30)"
  sleep 5
done
sleep 5

echo ""
echo "=== Step 5: Apply GeneratingPolicy with synchronize + generateExisting ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" apply -f - <<'POLICY'
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: sync-test-config
spec:
  evaluation:
    synchronize:
      enabled: true
    generateExisting:
      enabled: true
    orphanDownstreamOnPolicyDelete:
      enabled: true
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        resources: ["namespaces"]
        operations: [CREATE]
  matchConditions:
    - name: not-source
      expression: "object.metadata.name != 'source-ns'"
  variables:
    - name: targetNs
      expression: "object.metadata.name"
    - name: src
      expression: 'resource.Get("v1", "configmaps", "source-ns", "test-config")'
  generate:
    - expression: "generator.Apply(variables.targetNs, [variables.src])"
POLICY

echo ""
echo "=== Step 6: Wait for policy to be ready ==="
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  ready=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get generatingpolicies.policies.kyverno.io sync-test-config \
    -o jsonpath='{.status.conditionStatus.ready}' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$ready" = "true" ]; then
    echo "Policy ready (iteration $i)"
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done

echo ""
echo "=== Step 7: Create $NS_COUNT namespaces ==="
for i in $(seq 1 "$NS_COUNT"); do
  kubectl --context "$CTX" create ns "test-ns-$(printf '%03d' $i)" 2>/dev/null &
done
wait
echo "Created $NS_COUNT namespaces"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 8: Wait for clones to be generated ==="
echo "Waiting up to 120s for background controller to process all namespaces..."
for i in $(seq 1 24); do
  CLONE_COUNT=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm --all-namespaces \
    --field-selector metadata.name=test-config -o json \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys; items=json.load(sys.stdin)['items']; print(len([i for i in items if i['metadata']['namespace'] != 'source-ns']))")
  echo "  ($i/24) Clones: $CLONE_COUNT / $NS_COUNT"
  if [ "$CLONE_COUNT" -ge "$NS_COUNT" ]; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 5
done
echo "Clones found: $CLONE_COUNT / $NS_COUNT"

SAMPLE_NS=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm --all-namespaces \
  --field-selector metadata.name=test-config -o json \
  | python3 -c "import json,sys; items=json.load(sys.stdin)['items']; ns=[i['metadata']['namespace'] for i in items if i['metadata']['namespace'] != 'source-ns']; print(ns[0] if ns else '')")
if [ -z "$SAMPLE_NS" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: No clones were created at all"
  exit 1
fi
echo "Using sample namespace: $SAMPLE_NS"

echo ""
echo "=== Step 9: Verify sync works BEFORE restart ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" patch configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --type merge -p '{"data":{"key1":"pre-restart-update"}}'
echo "Source patched with key1=pre-restart-update"
echo "Waiting up to 30s for pre-restart sync..."
PRE_SYNCED=false
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  PRE_VAL=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$PRE_VAL" = "pre-restart-update" ]; then
    echo "PASS: Sync works before restart (iteration $i)"
    PRE_SYNCED=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 3
done
if [ "$PRE_SYNCED" != "true" ]; then
  echo "NOTE: Sync did not propagate within 30s before restart"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Step 10: Restart background controller ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" rollout restart deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno
kubectl --context "$CTX" rollout status deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno --timeout=60s
echo "Waiting 30s for controller to initialize..."
sleep 30

echo ""
echo "=== Step 11: Check watcher lifecycle after restart ==="
echo "--- Dynamic watcher events (ANSI stripped) ---"
kubectl --context "$CTX" logs deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno \
  | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
  | grep "processing generated\|start watcher\|watcher stopped\|Resource deleted\|Resource added\|Resource updated\|deleting downstream\|watcher already" \
  | head -40 || true
echo ""

echo ""
echo "=== Step 12: Test sync AFTER restart ==="
kubectl --context "$CTX" patch configmap test-config -n source-ns \
  --type merge -p '{"data":{"key1":"post-restart-update"}}'
echo "Source patched with key1=post-restart-update at $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
echo "Waiting up to 120s for propagation to $SAMPLE_NS..."
SYNCED=false
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  val=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ "$val" = "post-restart-update" ]; then
    echo "Sync propagated at $(date +%H:%M:%S) (iteration $i)"
    SYNCED=true
    break
  fi
  sleep 3
done

echo ""
echo "=== Results ==="
if [ "$SYNCED" = "true" ]; then
  echo "RESULT: Sync worked after restart — bug did NOT reproduce"
  echo "Try increasing NS_COUNT (current: $NS_COUNT) or adding background churn"
else
  POST_VAL=$(kubectl --context "$CTX" get cm test-config -n "$SAMPLE_NS" \
    -o jsonpath='{.data.key1}' 2>/dev/null || echo "MISSING")
  echo "RESULT: Sync FAILED after restart — bug REPRODUCED"
  echo "  Sample namespace: $SAMPLE_NS"
  echo "  Source has: key1=post-restart-update"
  echo "  Clone has:  key1=$POST_VAL"
  echo ""
  echo "--- Full watcher log (ANSI stripped) ---"
  kubectl --context "$CTX" logs deploy/kyverno-background-controller -n kyverno \
    | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' \
    | grep -E "dynamic_watcher|deleting downstream|processing generated|generate_controller|watcher stopped|watcher already" \
    | tail -50 || true
fi
```

</details>

## Expected behavior

1. All 50 clones should be created when `generateExisting: true` is set.
2. After restarting the background controller, source-change propagation should resume. Updating the source ConfigMap should propagate to all synchronized clones.
3. The dynamic watcher for `v1/configmaps` should remain alive (or be recreated) after processing UpdateRequests.

## Kyverno logs

Watcher lifecycle after the background controller restart shows rapid start/stop cycling — each UR processing iteration creates a watcher that immediately dies:

```
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC generate_controller.go:83 > start processing UR policy=sync-test-config ur=ur-cq4nr
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC generate_controller.go:83 > start processing UR policy=sync-test-config ur=ur-gddsj
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:339 > start watcher ... resourceVersion=2077
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:377 > Resource added  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:90  > watcher already exists for GVR gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps"
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:85  > processing generated resource gvr="/v1, Resource=configmaps" name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:339 > start watcher ... resourceVersion=2081
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:470 > Resource deleted  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2077
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z INF dynamic_watcher.go:470 > Resource deleted  name=test-config
2026-05-07T22:06:35Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2081
... (continues for ~20 iterations over 5 seconds, resourceVersion climbing 2077 → 2194)
2026-05-07T22:06:40Z TRC dynamic_watcher.go:371 > watcher stopped  resourceVersion=2194
```

Note the `watcher already exists for GVR` log line at `dynamic_watcher.go:90`. The dead entry from a previously stopped watcher is still in the `dynamicWatchers` map, so `SyncWatchers` skips creating a replacement.

After the final `watcher stopped`, no new watcher is ever created. No `Resource updated` events appear after the cycling completes — confirming the watcher is permanently dead and source changes are never observed.

title: [Bug] admissionController crashes due to unconditional v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy informer cache sync
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

### Description

The admission controller fails to start on Kubernetes 1.34+ because it unconditionally registers and waits for cache sync of `v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy`, which was promoted to v1beta1 in Kubernetes 1.34. The controller exits with a fatal error regardless of the --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy flag value.

To Reproduce

Run Kyverno chart v3.7.2 (v1.17.2) on a Kubernetes 1.34 cluster
Observe admission controller pod stuck in 0/1 / CrashLoopBackOff

The admission controller should either:

Conditionally register the MutatingAdmissionPolicy informer only when --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=true, or
Use v1beta1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy on clusters that serve it (with version discovery), or
Gracefully skip cache sync for APIs not served by the cluster


In my setup, the admission controller crashes at startup:
```

ERR k8s.io/client-go@v0.35.1/tools/cache/reflector.go:204 > Failed to watch error="failed to list *v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy: the server could not find the requested resource"
ERR k8s.io/client-go@v0.35.1/tools/cache/reflector.go:204 > Failed to watch error="failed to list *v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding: the server could not find the requested resource"
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/internal/informer.go:30 > failed to wait for cache sync type=*v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/internal/informer.go:30 > failed to wait for cache sync type=*v1alpha1.MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
ERR github.com/kyverno/kyverno/cmd/kyverno/main.go:634 > failed to wait for cache sync error="failed to wait for cache sync"
```

Note that the feature flag has no effect. With --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=false the informer is still registered and the cache sync is still waited on:

```
$ kubectl get deploy -n kyverno kyverno-admission-controller -o yaml | grep -i generate
        - --generateValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true
        - --generateMutatingAdmissionPolicy=false
```


I can see that this was also reported on the community Slack channel twice:

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1773749540483199

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1771597927193229

I was supposed to be fixed in v1.17.2 by https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/15364, but I think that this change was not cherry picked (https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pull/15799#issuecomment-4225272525)

With Kyverno v1.18, the deployment works fine, on the same setup.

Cherry picking the changes would probably solve the issue. 

### Slack discussion

https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1773749540483199, https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/CLGR9BJU9/p1771597927193229

title: [Bug] Leader election starved by global client-go rate limits during cold start with multiple replicas of admission controller
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.2

### Description

## Summary

Kyverno controller pods enter CrashLoopBackOff after a `kubectl rollout restart` when running multiple replicas. The pods successfully acquire the leader lease but lose it ~36 seconds later because informer LIST bursts exhaust the shared client-go rate limiter, preventing lease renewal PUT requests from executing within their context deadline.

## Environment

- Cloud Provider: AKS
- Kyverno version: `v1.17.1`
- Replicas: 3 per controller (admission-controller, controlled by HPA with `minReplicas=3`)
- CRD count: ~15+ Kyverno CRD types, ~1936 policyreports, plus admissionreports, backgroundscanreports, ephemeralreports, etc.

## How to Reproduce

This is admittedly not super straightforward to reproduce on a laptop with something like `kind`. I think you could drop `--clientRateLimitQPS` to something around 2-5 and `--clientRateLimitBurst` to 10-20, then:

- Run 3 replicas
- Install a large volume of policies and get the Informer to register a high volume of watches on the API
- Run `kubectl rollout restart` on the admission controller Deployment

## Symptoms

```
2026-04-29T22:31:31Z TRC starting controller name=ttl-controller-manager workers=3
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z ERR Failed to update lease optimistically, falling back to slow path
    error="Put \"https://10.0.0.1:443/.../leases/kyverno-cleanup-controller\": context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z ERR Error retrieving lease lock
    error="client rate limiter Wait returned an error: context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z INF Failed to renew lease err="context deadline exceeded"
2026-04-29T22:32:07Z TRC leadership lost, stopped leading
```

In that 30-something second period, there appears to be a large burst in QPS that occurs, at which point the leader lease is lost.

## Workarounds

For now, it's probably just increasing the values for `clientRateLimitQPS` and `clientRateLimitBurst`

title: [Bug] reports-controller ClusterRole missing list/watch on CRDs — global.crdWatcher has no effect on reports-controller
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

## Describe the bug

After upgrading to v1.17, the `reports-controller` leader pod emits a burst of RBAC-denied errors for `customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io` immediately after acquiring the leader lease. The errors repeat rapidly for a few seconds then stop — they recur on every pod restart.

**Error logs (leader pod, immediately after acquiring lease):**

```
{"level":"info","logger":"klog","lock":"kyverno/kyverno-reports-controller","message":"Successfully acquired lease"}
{"level":"error","gvr":"apiextensions.k8s.io/v1, Resource=customresourcedefinitions","gvk":"apiextensions.k8s.io/v1, Kind=CustomResourceDefinition","error":"customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-reports-controller\" cannot list resource \"customresourcedefinitions\" in API group \"apiextensions.k8s.io\" at the cluster scope","logger":"resource-report-controller","message":"failed to list resources"}
{"level":"error","gvr":"apiextensions.k8s.io/v1, Resource=customresourcedefinitions","gvk":"apiextensions.k8s.io/v1, Kind=CustomResourceDefinition","error":"customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kyverno:kyverno-reports-controller\" cannot list resource \"customresourcedefinitions\" in API group \"apiextensions.k8s.io\" at the cluster scope","logger":"resource-report-controller","message":"failed to start watcher"}
```

_(The above pair repeats ~10 times over ~3 seconds, then stops.)_

---

## Root cause

The `:core` ClusterRole for the `reports-controller` only grants `get` on CRDs:

```yaml
# charts/kyverno/templates/reports-controller/clusterrole.yaml
- apiGroups:
    - apiextensions.k8s.io
  resources:
    - customresourcedefinitions
  verbs:
    - get   # list and watch are missing
```

When a policy targets `kind: CustomResourceDefinition`, the `resource-report-controller` attempts to open a `list`/`watch` informer on CRDs to dynamically discover resource types for report generation. This fails because the ClusterRole does not grant those verbs.

---

## Inconsistency with `global.crdWatcher`

PR #13141 wired up a `crdWatcher` flag for the `admissionController` that conditionally adds `list`/`watch` on CRDs to its ClusterRole:

```yaml
# charts/kyverno/templates/admission-controller/clusterrole.yaml
- apiGroups:
    - apiextensions.k8s.io
  resources:
    - customresourcedefinitions
  verbs:
    - get
    {{- if .Values.admissionController.crdWatcher | default .Values.global.crdWatcher }}
    - list
    - watch
    {{- end }}
```

The `reports-controller` ClusterRole template has **no equivalent conditional**. Setting `global.crdWatcher: true` has no effect on the reports-controller — it still only receives `get`. We confirmed this by rendering the chart locally with `global.crdWatcher=true`.

---

## Reproduction

1. Deploy Kyverno v1.17 with any policy that targets `kind: CustomResourceDefinition` in its match block
2. Restart the `reports-controller` deployment
3. Observe RBAC-denied errors in the leader pod logs immediately after `Successfully acquired lease`

Clusters with no CRD-targeting policies do **not** exhibit this behavior.

---

## Expected behavior

Either:
- Setting `global.crdWatcher: true` (or `reportsController.crdWatcher: true`) should also grant `list`/`watch` on CRDs to the reports-controller, consistent with how it works for the admission-controller, **or**
- `list` and `watch` should be added unconditionally to the existing CRD rule in the reports-controller ClusterRole, since the `resource-report-controller` already attempts this regardless of the `crdWatcher` flag

---

## Suggested fix

Apply the same conditional to `charts/kyverno/templates/reports-controller/clusterrole.yaml`:

```yaml
- apiGroups:
    - apiextensions.k8s.io
  resources:
    - customresourcedefinitions
  verbs:
    - get
    {{- if .Values.reportsController.crdWatcher | default .Values.global.crdWatcher }}
    - list
    - watch
    {{- end }}
```

---

## Workaround

Until this is fixed upstream, `list`/`watch` can be added via `reportsController.rbac.coreClusterRole.extraResources`:

```yaml
reportsController:
  rbac:
    coreClusterRole:
      extraResources:
        - apiGroups:
            - apiextensions.k8s.io
          resources:
            - customresourcedefinitions
          verbs:
            - list
            - watch
```

---

## Version
- Kyverno: v1.17.2
- Chart: kyverno-3.7.1

title: [Bug] generateExisting and synchronize fail when update requests are too large for kubernetes database
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Description

In very large clusters `generateExisting` and `synchronize` policies that apply to a large number of objects will create very large `UpdateRequest`s that cannot be applied.

I believe that updates need to be batched into multiple `UpdateRequest`s when a large number of objects need to be created/modified.

A minimal example to quickly reproduce this:

Install kyverno:
```bash
helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/kyverno/
helm repo update
helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace
```

Create many namespaces:
```bash
N=10000

for i in $(seq -w 1 "$N"); do
  kubectl create namespace test-ns-${i} || true
done
```

Apply the following policy that generates a `ConfigMap` in every namespace:
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: generate-configmap-all-namespaces
spec:
  generateExisting: true
  rules:
    - name: generate-example-configmap
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Namespace
      generate:
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: ConfigMap
        name: example-configmap
```

title: [Bug] GlobalContextEntry created after admission controller startup is never loaded
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.15.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.32.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

Validate

### Description

When a new `GlobalContextEntry` (GCE) is created while Kyverno controller pods are already running, the dynamic informer for the new GCE's backing resource is never created. The controller logs `"no built-in informer found, use dynamic informer"` once at GCE creation time, then goes completely silent — no list/watch calls are ever made for the new resource. Every subsequent policy evaluation returns `"global context entry not found, returning nil"`.
A rolling restart of the affected controller deployment loads the GCE correctly at startup alongside all others.

Similar, previously closed: https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/13871

### Steps to reproduce

## Setup
- **Kyverno**: v1.15.1 (Helm chart)
- **Kubernetes**: EKS 1.32, multiple clusters
- **Affected controller**: admission-controller (3-replica deployment, pods running 45–69 days)
- **Pre-existing GCEs**: 10 other GlobalContextEntries, all loaded at startup, all working correctly

## Steps to reproduce
-  Verify the GCE resource is created successfully (kubectl get globalcontextentry)
- Create a policy (ClusterPolicy or ValidatingPolicy) that references the new GCE via globalReference or globalContext.Get()
- Observe admission-controller logs — the GCE is never resolved
- Check API server audit log, zero list/watch calls from the kyverno service account for the new GCE's GVR

### Expected behavior

A newly created `GlobalContextEntry` should be dynamically loaded by all running Kyverno controller pods (admission-controller, reports-controller, etc.) without requiring a pod restart. The controller should:
- Detect the new GCE resource via its watch on `GlobalContextEntry` objects
- Create a dynamic informer for the backing Kubernetes resource (list + watch)


### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell
# === At GCE creation time (logged once, then silence) ===
{"level":"debug","logger":"global-context","gvr":"example.io/v1alpha1, Resource=customresources","message":"no built-in informer found, use dynamic informer"}


On every subsequent webhook call (repeats indefinitely) ===


{"level":"trace","entry":"customresources","message":"global context entry not found, returning nil"}


API server audit logs (corroborating evidence) ===


# Kyverno SA has active list/watch for all GCE-backed resources loaded at startup (pytorchjobs, etc.)
# Zero list/watch calls for example.io/v1alpha1/customresources — informer was never created
# === After rolling restart — all GCEs load correctly, zero "entry not found" errors ===
```

title: [Feature] [Refactor] Proper Context Propagation in Policy Controller
body:
### Problem Statement

The synchronous event handlers `updatePolicy` and `deletePolicy` in `pkg/policy/policy_controller.go` currently use `context.Background()` instead of the controller's lifecycle context. This bypasses Kyverno's lifecycle management and cancellation signals. Proper context propagation ensures that shutdown signals are respected, improves maintainability by following Go best practices, and enables better observability through tracing.

### Solution Description

Capture the lifecycle context provided in the `Run` method of the `policyController` and propagate it to the synchronous event handlers (`updatePolicy`, `deletePolicy`) and downstream resource operations. This ensure Kyverno's lifecycle management and cancellation signals are correctly followed throughout the package.

title: [Bug] ValidatingPolicy/MutatingPolicy webhook configuration updated every reconciliation cycle due to non-deterministic webhook ordering ?
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.1

### Kubernetes Version

1.33.x

### Kubernetes Platform

GKE

### Kyverno Rule Type

Validate

### Description

# Title

ValidatingPolicy/MutatingPolicy webhook configuration updated every reconciliation cycle due to non-deterministic webhook ordering

# Body

## Description

After deploying CEL-based ValidatingPolicies (`policies.kyverno.io/v1`), the `kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg` ValidatingWebhookConfiguration is updated every ~15 seconds even when no policy changes have occurred. This causes policy `ready` status to oscillate between `true` and `false` when observed via `kubectl get -w`.

## Root Cause

The fine-grained webhook entries (one per policy with `matchConditions`) are written in non-deterministic order on each reconciliation cycle. This appears to be caused by Go map iteration ordering in the webhook construction code (`pkg/controllers/webhook/validating.go`).

Each cycle produces the same set of webhooks but in a different order → Kubernetes API server sees a change → increments `resourceVersion` → Kyverno detects the version change → reconciles again → infinite loop.

Additionally, `pkg/controllers/webhook/controller.go` in `reconcileValidatingWebhookConfiguration()` performs an unconditional update without comparing old vs new configuration.

## Evidence

### Webhook ordering changes every ~15 seconds

5 consecutive captures of the webhook names show the same 12 `finegrained` entries in different order each time:

```
Snapshot 1: policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, ...
Snapshot 2: policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, policy-a, ...
Snapshot 3: policy-d, policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, ...
Snapshot 4: policy-a, policy-b, policy-c, policy-d, ...
Snapshot 5: policy-c, policy-a, policy-b, policy-d, ...
```

The first webhook (`validate.kyverno.svc-ignore`) and last two (`vpol...fail`, `vpol...ignore`) remain stable. Only the `finegrained` entries shuffle.

### Prometheus confirms continuous changes

```promql
sum by(cluster)(changes(kube_validatingwebhookconfiguration_metadata_resource_version{validatingwebhookconfiguration="kyverno-resource-validating-webhook-cfg"}[5m]))
```

Results over 30 days:
- **Before deploying ValidatingPolicies, we were on clusterpolicies**: 0 changes per 5 minutes
- **After deploying ValidatingPolicies**: 4 changes per 5 minutes (constant, 24/7)

### Enforcement is NOT affected

64 consecutive enforcement tests over 2 minutes during the oscillation period — all correctly blocked. The webhook stays registered regardless of status flapping.

## Environment

- Kyverno: v1.17.1
- Kubernetes: 1.33.x
- Number of ValidatingPolicies: ~30
- Number of MutatingPolicies: ~7
- Admission controller replicas: 3

## Expected Behavior

The webhook configuration should not be updated when no policies have changed. The `ready` status should remain stable at `true`.


## Impact

- **Enforcement**: Not sure it is impacted when status changes
- **API server load**: ~4 unnecessary writes/min per cluster
- **Monitoring**: Status flapping triggers false alerts
- **User confusion**: `ready: false` appears intermittently when watching policies


### Steps to reproduce

Deploy multiple validatingpolicy in cluster and try to see if policy status flaps

### Expected behavior

constant flapping should not happen

```Shell

```

The issue template forces me to enter a version, but I've actually tested this against the current main, which already includes the recent fixes for referencing the trigger object inside `mutations` expressions.

title: [Bug] Admission controller serves stale policy cache after watch stream failure until lease timeout
[Bug] leaderelection.New calls os.Exit(1) instead of returning error when leader elector creation fails
body:
## Kyverno Version

1.15.x (main branch)

## Description

In [pkg/leaderelection/leaderelection.go](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/leaderelection/leaderelection.go#L104-L108) at lines 104–108, when `leaderelection.NewLeaderElector()` fails, the code calls `os.Exit(1)` instead of returning the error to the caller:

```go
e.leaderElector, err = leaderelection.NewLeaderElector(e.leaderElectionCfg)
if err != nil {
    e.log.Error(err, "failed to create leaderElector")
    os.Exit(1)  // ← BUG: should return error, not terminate the process
}
```

This is inconsistent with the rest of New() which correctly returns errors (for example, the `resourcelock.New` error at lines 62–64). Calling `os.Exit(1)` inside a library constructor has serious consequences:

- **No graceful shutdown** — skips deferred cleanups, in-flight request handling, and telemetry flushing
- **Untestable** — any misconfiguration in tests causes the entire test process to exit abruptly
- **Violates Go conventions** — library functions must never call `os.Exit`; errors must be propagated to the caller
- **Caller is bypassed** — New() already returns (Interface, error), so callers are prepared to handle errors but never get the chance

## Expected Behavior

The error should be returned to the caller:

```go
e.leaderElector, err = leaderelection.NewLeaderElector(e.leaderElectionCfg)
if err != nil {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create leader elector: %w", err)
}
```

This allows callers to perform graceful shutdown, makes the code fully testable, and follows standard Go error-handling conventions. The now-unused `os` import can also be removed.

title: [Bug] [CLI] kyverno apply cannot clone GitLab repositories that are located in nested groups/subgroups.
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0

### Description

kyverno apply cannot clone GitLab repositories that are located in nested groups/subgroups.
The CLI assumes that every Git repository URL follows the pattern:

`https://<host>/<owner>/<repository>`
When a GitLab repository contains multiple nested groups, the repository URL is truncated to the first two path segments before cloning.
For example, given the repository URL:
https://gitlab.example.com/group/subgroup/team/project.git
the CLI attempts to clone:
https://gitlab.example.com/group/subgroup
instead of the full repository URL.
The issue appears to originate from the following code:

`pathElems := strings.Split(gitSourceURL.Path[1:], "/")
gitSourceURL.Path = strings.Join([]string{pathElems[0], pathElems[1]}, "/")
repoURL := gitSourceURL.String()`

As a result, cloning fails with:

Although the credentials are valid, the repository URL used for cloning is incorrect.

A same bug was opened here:
https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/issues/12513

Create a private GitLab repository located in nested groups, for example:
https://gitlab.example.com/group/subgroup/team/project.git
2. Verify that the repository can be cloned successfully using Git:

title: [Bug] [CLI] `kubectl kyverno apply --cluster` fails to match resources containing hyphens in name, namespace, or API group
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description


### Description
In `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/utils/common/fetch.go`, `getFromCluster()` filters cluster resources requested via `--resource` (`-r`) by splitting a synthesized lookup key `rn` using `strings.Split(rn, "-")` and checking if `s[2] == resourcePath`.

Because hyphens (`-`) are valid characters in Kubernetes resource names (e.g., `my-deployment`), namespace names (e.g., `kube-system`), and API group names (e.g., `cert-manager.io`), `strings.Split` splits the key into more than 3 elements:

1. **Hyphenated Resource Name**: For a resource named `my-deployment` in namespace `default`, `rn` is `"Deployment-default-my-deployment"`. `strings.Split(rn, "-")` yields `["Deployment", "default", "my", "deployment"]`. `s[2]` evaluates to `"my"`, so `"my" == "my-deployment"` is `false`.
2. **Hyphenated Namespace**: For a resource `pod1` in namespace `kube-system`, `rn` is `"Pod-kube-system-pod1"`. `strings.Split(rn, "-")` yields `["Pod", "kube", "system", "pod1"]`. `s[2]` evaluates to `"system"`, which is part of the namespace name, failing the match.
3. **Hyphenated API Group in Concurrent Mode**: In concurrent mode (`--concurrency > 1`), `rn` is constructed using `resource.GroupVersionKind()` (e.g. `"cert-manager.io/v1, Kind=Certificate-default-mycert"`). Hyphens in the group name shift index 2 to point to the namespace rather than the resource name.

As a result, `kubectl kyverno apply --cluster -r <resource_name>` fails with `resource <resource_name> not found in cluster` even when the resource exists in the cluster.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Deploy a resource with a hyphen in its name (e.g., a Deployment named `my-app` in namespace `default`) to a Kubernetes cluster.
2. Run `kubectl kyverno apply --policy policy.yaml --cluster -r my-app`.
3. Observe the CLI failure: `resource my-app not found in cluster`.

### Expected behavior
`kubectl kyverno apply --cluster` should correctly match and filter resources from the cluster regardless of whether their names, namespaces, or API groups contain hyphens.

title: [Feature] CEL Policy Decision Explainability
body:
### Problem Statement

# Summary

Kyverno's CEL engine runs a whole pipeline on the way to an admit or deny (scope filtering, match conditions, variables, validation expressions, autogen rule expansion, mutation, exception handling) and discards the per-expression detail the moment it has a final answer. When a CEL policy does something surprising (matches a resource you didn't expect, skips one you did, denies with a message that doesn't say which clause fired, or fails with a bare `"no such key"`), there is no supported way to see which sub-expression produced which value. This proposes an opt-in, structured decision trace: capture what the engine already computes, once, in a stable machine-readable form, and surface it where users look (the CLI first, then reports and the running controller). It broadens KDP [#91](https://github.com/kyverno/KDP/pull/91) from a two-phase CLI-plus-runtime feature into a decision-explainability primitive for the whole CEL pipeline.

# Background and motivation

The recurring pain is "my CEL policy did something and I can't see why." A sample of the issues behind it:

- #15353: a `MutatingPolicy` produced nothing, and the reporter spent hours at verbosity 5 with nothing useful (closed by stale-bot, not fixed).
- #16023: a CEL policy the reporter called impossible to debug even at `-v=6` (open).
- #15949: offline CLI evaluation of CEL policies (already addressed, noted here for honesty).

To be straight about the shape of the demand: it is real but spread across many small issues rather than one loud one. The single highest-voted nearby item (#9804,) is a CLI false-positive correctness bug, not strictly a runtime-explainability request, . The consistent thread across the smaller issues is the absence of a first-class way to inspect a CEL decision.

The `kyverno.io` troubleshooting docs confirm the gap: for CEL policies they offer `dumpPayload` and `-v=4`, with no per-expression view.

One overlap to name up front so this doesn't read as duplicate work: PR #16104 (`ivpol`) and #16061 (image verification) add `V(4)`/`V(6)` log lines. Those help a maintainer tailing the controller, but they are scattered high-verbosity logs, not a structured, low-verbosity, user-facing record attached to the decision. This proposal is the latter, and it works offline from the CLI without a running cluster.

# Related

- KDP #74 ("kyverno trace") proposed something adjacent but is stale (untouched for roughly 14 months) and aspirational, with no evaluation mechanics. It shows an independent contributor wanted this; #91 is the grounded design that subsumes it.
- OPA (`opa eval --explain full`, `opa test --var-values`, Gatekeeper's `gator --trace`) does real per-expression value tracing, but for Rego, at dev time on the CLI, as a raw firehose rather than a curated decision record.
- Kubernetes `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` surfaces `expressionIndex` plus a message through an audit annotation, but no intermediate values, and points users to the CEL playground.
- `cel-go` has the primitive for this (`OptTrackState`), and every consumer discards it. The CEL playground uses cost tracking, not state tracking; the CEL REPL shows only the final value. Kyverno itself discards `*cel.EvalDetails` at every call site.

So per-expression, curated, decision-attached explainability spanning scope through mutation and exceptions is unbuilt anywhere .

# The design

Capture what the engine already computes, once, as a versioned structured record (`trace.kyverno.io/v1alpha1`), with a uniform per-expression shape (source text, resolved value, provenance) organized in layers so cheap information is always available and expensive information stays opt-in:

1. **Scope:** did the policy apply, and if not, which constraint (kind, namespace, selector) filtered it out.
2. **Match:** each match condition with its resolved boolean.
3. **Variables:** each declared variable and the value it resolved to (the layer people most often can't get today).
4. **Verdict:** each validation expression with its result and the message that would fire.
5. **Autogen provenance:** for an auto-generated rule (Deployment, DaemonSet, and so on), which original pod-level rule it came from.
6. **Mutation:** the before and after of the object, plus which mutation expressions ran.
7. **Exception:** if a `PolicyException` applied, which one.
8. **Errors:** evaluation errors attached to the sub-expression that raised them, instead of a bare `"no such key"`.

Illustrative CLI output:

```text
$ kyverno explain --policy require-labels.yaml --resource pod.yaml

Policy: require-labels (ValidatingPolicy)
Resource: Pod/nginx (namespace: prod)

SCOPE      applied   matched kind Pod, namespace prod
MATCH      true      object.metadata.namespace == 'prod'   ->  true
VARIABLES  hasTeam   has(object.metadata.labels.team)      ->  false
VERDICT    FAIL      has(object.metadata.labels.team)      ->  false
                     message: "every pod must carry a team label"
```



### Solution Description

Ordered by implementation certainty, not ambition, so the earliest phases are the ones already confirmed low-risk against the code.

### Phase 1 (decision-trace core plus CLI)

The trace data structure, a `kyverno explain` command, and an `--explain` flag on `test` and `apply`. Offline and opt-in. Uses `cel-go`'s `OptTrackState` only inside the CLI invocation, where the cost does not touch the admission path. This is the slice to prototype for a maintainer meeting. (The in-repo `jp` command is a precedent for a CLI command that evaluates CEL.)

### Phase 2 (full-pipeline depth)

Fill in the remaining layers, in increasing order of plumbing cost: exception attribution first (already computed by the engine), then autogen provenance (the autogen functions are pure), then scope filtering, then mutation (feasible but structural, see below).

### Phase 3 (runtime, gated)

Produce the same trace from the running controller for a single flagged admission request or policy, as an event or a low-verbosity log. Gated on benchmarking, because turning on state tracking in the admission hot path has a cost that is not yet quantified. If the benchmark says no, Phases 1, 2, and 4 still stand.

### Phase 4 (platform primitive)

Carry a compact form of the trace into `PolicyReport` and `openreports` result `Properties`, reusing the existing pattern of stashing structured JSON there, so the "why" travels with the "what".

### Phase 5 (stretch, explicitly speculative)

A playground view that renders the trace, and optionally emitting it as OpenTelemetry span attributes.

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional Context

# Feasibility

Checked against current `main`:

- Single insertion point: `pkg/cel/compiler/compiler.go` compiles then builds the program (`env.Compile` then `env.Program`) and discards the AST. Retaining the AST and passing `cel.EvalOptions(cel.OptTrackState)` is one localized change, not four.
- Every policy compiler under `pkg/cel/policies/{vpol,mpol,gpol,dpol}/compiler` already calls `ContextEval` and drops the returned `*cel.EvalDetails`, so the state is computed and thrown away today.
- `cel-go` (v0.29.2) exposes what's needed: `EvalDetails.State().IDs()` and `Value(id)`, plus `SourceInfo.GetOffsetRange(id)` and `GetStartLocation(id)` to map a node back to source, rendered via `cel.ExprToString` (not byte slicing, which undercounts whitespace on composite nodes).
- Exception attribution is already in the engine result, and reports already copy result `Properties` into the `PolicyReport`, so Phase 4 needs no new report plumbing.
- Autogen provenance is pure-function territory (`pkg/cel/policies/{vpol,mpol,ivpol}/autogen`); `gpol` and `dpol` have no autogen, so this layer is scoped to `vpol`, `mpol`, and `ivpol`.
- Honest limits: the matcher currently returns a bare bool (`pkg/cel/matching/matcher.go`), so scope explanation is net-new derivation (bounded, since the matcher is inspectable). Mutation is a whole-object before/after diff (`pkg/cel/policies/mpol/engine/engine.go`), so one-to-one op-to-expression attribution is a stretch; showing the diff plus which mutation expressions ran is the realistic target.

# Scope and non-goals

- Not a metrics feature. Kyverno already registers policy-result metrics; this is the per-decision "why" dimension, not aggregate counters.
- Not always-on. The trace is opt-in everywhere; the runtime path stays behind a flag and a benchmark.
- Not a replacement for `kyverno test`; it complements it by explaining a single evaluation.

title: [Bug] ext/file: IsYaml and IsJson extension checks are case-sensitive
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.16.4

### Description


In `ext/file/ext.go`, the extension checkers `IsYaml` and `IsJson` perform case-sensitive checks against `.yaml`, `.yml`, and `.json`. 

```
go
func IsYaml(path string) bool {
	ext := filepath.Ext(path)
	return ext == ".yml" || ext == ".yaml"
}
```

If a file ends in .YAML, .YML, or .JSON, these functions return false.

Why we need to solve this:

When Kyverno CLI tools (like kubectl-kyverno) load directories containing policies and resource manifests, they filter files using IsYaml Or Json. Files ending in uppercase extensions are silently skipped. Normalizing extensions to lowercase before checking prevents these load failures.

Proposed Fix:
Use strings.ToLower on the extracted extension:

```
go
func IsYaml(path string) bool {
	ext := strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path))
	return ext == ".yml" || ext == ".yaml"
}

```

title: [Feature] : Support Kubernetes subresources and operations in CEL engine requests
body:
### Problem Statement

The CLI currently constructs CEL admission requests using hardcoded values for the admission operation (`CREATE`) and subresource (`""`) when evaluating policies.

As a result, CEL policies that depend on `request.operation` or target Kubernetes subresources (such as `status` or `scale`) cannot be accurately evaluated through the CLI, even though these attributes are available in real admission requests.

### Solution Description

Update the CLI policy processor to construct `celengine.Request()` using the actual simulated request context instead of hardcoded values.

Specifically:

- Resolve the admission operation from the CLI request variables, defaulting to `CREATE` if unspecified.
- Pass the computed subresource instead of an empty string.
- Use these values consistently for both mutating and validating policy evaluation.

This would allow the CLI to more closely match the behavior of Kyverno running inside a Kubernetes cluster.

### Alternatives

The current implementation always uses `CREATE` and an empty subresource, which simplifies request construction but limits the CLI's ability to accurately simulate admission requests for CEL policies.

Another alternative is to continue documenting this limitation, but supporting the actual request context provides a more accurate and consistent testing experience.

### Additional Context


Supporting these request attributes would improve parity between CLI policy evaluation and in-cluster admission processing, particularly for CEL policies that rely on `request.operation` or target Kubernetes subresources.

### Kyverno CLI Version

### Description

When running `kyverno test`, cluster-scoped resources are displayed with an extra slash (`//`) in the resource column.

For example:

```text
v1/ClusterRole//cluster-admin
```

This happens because the resource key is generated as:

```text
v1,ClusterRole,,cluster-admin
```

During output formatting, all commas are replaced with `/`, which results in a double slash when the namespace is empty.

Cluster-scoped resources should instead be displayed as:

```text
v1/ClusterRole/cluster-admin
```

Namespace-scoped resources should continue to display normally.

Cluster-scoped resources should be formatted without an empty namespace component.

title: [Feature] Support JSON/YAML output for the version command
body:
### Problem Statement

The kyverno version command currently outputs version information only in a human-readable text format. While suitable for interactive use, this output is difficult to parse reliably in scripts, CI/CD pipelines, and other automation workflows.

Supporting structured output formats would make the command easier to consume programmatically and align it with common Kubernetes CLI conventions.

### Solution Description

Add support for an -o / --output flag to the version command.

Supported formats:

Default (no flag): retain the existing plain text output.
-o json: print version information in JSON format.
-o yaml: print version information in YAML format.

If an unsupported output format is provided, return a descriptive error indicating the supported values.

This change maintains backward compatibility while enabling structured output for automation.

### Alternatives

Users can currently parse the plain text output using shell utilities such as grep, awk, or sed, but these approaches are fragile and can break if the output format changes. Providing native JSON and YAML output is a more robust and standard solution.

### Additional Context

This enhancement improves the usability of the Kyverno CLI for automation, scripting, and CI/CD workflows. It also aligns the version command with the output formatting conventions used by Kubernetes tools such as kubectl version -o json.

title: [Bug] [CLI] OCI annotations should use the policy API version instead of a hardcoded value
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0

### Description

When generating OCI metadata for a Kyverno policy, the `io.kyverno.image.apiVersion` annotation is always emitted as `kyverno.io/v1`, regardless of the API version stored on the policy object.

The current implementation hardcodes the annotation value instead of deriving it from the policy being packaged.

As a result, the generated OCI metadata can become inconsistent with the packaged policy if a different API version is used.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `Policy` or `ClusterPolicy` object with an API version different from the hardcoded `kyverno.io/v1` (this can be reproduced in a unit test by constructing the object with a different `TypeMeta.APIVersion`).
2. Generate the OCI annotations.
3. Observe that `io.kyverno.image.apiVersion` is always emitted as:

```text
kyverno.io/v1
```

instead of the policy object's API version.

### Expected behavior

The value of `io.kyverno.image.apiVersion` should always match the policy object's `apiVersion`.

For example, if the policy object has:

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v2beta1
kind: ClusterPolicy
```

the generated annotation should be:

```text
io.kyverno.image.apiVersion=kyverno.io/v2beta1
```

rather than the hardcoded `kyverno.io/v1`.

## Additional Context
The current implementation in `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/oci/internal/annotations.go` hardcodes:

```go
AnnotationApiVersion: "kyverno.io/v1"
```

instead of deriving the value from the policy object.
