title: [Bug] [CLI] Remote HTTP policy/resource loads can hang indefinitely
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version
1.18.0

### Description
## Summary
The CLI supports loading policies and resources from HTTP URLs, but the remote fetch paths are unbounded. `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/policy/load.go` and `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/resource/resource.go` build requests with `context.TODO()` and send them with `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout by default. A slow or blackholed endpoint can therefore block `kubectl-kyverno apply` or `kubectl-kyverno test` indefinitely.

## Affected Area
- `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/policy`
- `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/resource`
- CLI HTTP URL loading for policies and resources

### Steps to reproduce
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Point `kubectl-kyverno apply` or `kubectl-kyverno test` at an HTTP URL for a policy or resource.
2. Make that endpoint accept the connection but never finish the response, or otherwise stall long enough to avoid completion.
3. Follow the code path through `policy.httpLoad()` or `resource.GetFileBytes()`.
4. Observe that the request uses `http.NewRequestWithContext(context.TODO(), ...)` and `http.DefaultClient.Do(req)` with no request timeout.
5. Observe that the CLI can hang indefinitely waiting for the remote endpoint.

### Expected behavior
## Expected Behaviour
Remote policy and resource loading should use a bounded timeout and a cancellable context so the CLI fails predictably instead of hanging forever.

### Screenshots
Not applicable for this code-path issue.

### Kyverno logs
## Technical Evidence
```text
cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/policy/load.go
- http.NewRequestWithContext(context.TODO(), http.MethodGet, path, nil)
- http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/resource/resource.go
- http.NewRequestWithContext(context.TODO(), http.MethodGet, path, nil)
- http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
```

### Slack discussion
Not applicable.

### Troubleshooting
- [x] I have read and followed the [troubleshooting guide](https://kyverno.io/docs/troubleshooting/).
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

## Actual Behaviour
A remote policy or resource URL can stall the CLI indefinitely because these fetch paths do not apply any timeout or caller cancellation.

## Suspected Root Cause
The CLI remote loader paths rely on the global default HTTP client and a placeholder request context instead of a timeout-configured client and propagated command context.

## Proposed Direction
Introduce a shared timeout-configured HTTP client for CLI remote fetches and thread context through the policy/resource loader entry points used by the CLI commands.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Remote policy and resource fetches fail within a documented timeout on slow or non-responsive endpoints.
- Unit tests cover timeout and non-200 HTTP responses for both loader paths.
- Existing successful HTTP loading behavior remains intact.

title: [Bug] [CLI] infer request.operation from request context in policy evaluation
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0 (also present on `main` as reviewed on 2026-07-07)

### Description

## Summary
Offline CLI policy evaluation can mis-handle `UPDATE` and `DELETE` scenarios when the simulated admission request is supplied through JSON context rather than through resolved variables. In `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go`, `makePolicyContext()` defaults the operation to `CREATE` and only switches away from it by reading `resourceValues["request.operation"]`.

## Affected Area
`cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor`, especially `makePolicyContext()` in `policy_processor.go`.

## Technical Evidence
- `makePolicyContext()` contains an inline TODO stating the current behavior is buggy and should read the operation from the JSON context.
- The current switch reads `resourceValues["request.operation"]`, so `request.oldObject` and related request JSON can already be present in the JSON context while the admission operation still remains `CREATE`.
- Later in the same function, the code reconstructs `request.object` and `request.oldObject` from the JSON context, which means the operation source is out of sync with the rest of the request payload.

## Suspected Root Cause
Admission operation detection is coupled to computed variable resolution instead of the normalized request JSON context.

## Proposed Direction
Infer `request.operation` from the assembled JSON context (and still honor explicit overrides when present there), then keep the existing logic that rebuilds `request.object` and `request.oldObject` from that same context.

## Acceptance Criteria
- CLI `test` and `apply` correctly evaluate `UPDATE` and `DELETE` scenarios from request context alone.
- Regression tests cover operation inference from request context without requiring a values-file workaround.
- Existing `CREATE` behavior remains unchanged.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a CLI test or apply scenario for a policy whose behavior differs on `UPDATE` or `DELETE`.
2. Provide `request.oldObject` or equivalent request context through the request JSON/context path, but do not rely on a variables file that sets `request.operation`.
3. Run `kubectl-kyverno test ...` or `kubectl-kyverno apply ...`.
4. Observe that the policy context still uses `CREATE`, matching the current code path in `policy_processor.go`.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should infer the admission operation from the request JSON context or explicit simulated request input, not only from computed variable values.

### Screenshots

Not applicable.

### Kyverno logs

Static verification point in `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go`:

// TODO: this is kind of buggy, we should read that from the json context

title: [Bug] [CLI] kyverno apply --audit-warn treats ValidatingPolicy audit violations as failures
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0

### Description

`kyverno apply --audit-warn` correctly treats legacy `Policy` and `ClusterPolicy` audit violations as warnings: they are counted under `warn`, and the process exits `0` when there are no enforced failures.

The same behavior does not apply to CEL `ValidatingPolicy` resources from `policies.kyverno.io/v1`. When a `ValidatingPolicy` has `spec.validationActions: Audit`, a validation failure is printed as an audit warning but is still counted as `fail`, causing `kyverno apply` to exit `1`

### Steps to reproduce

Create `policy.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: audit
spec:
  validationActions:
    - Audit
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  validations:
    - expression: "false"
      message: audit failure
```

Create `pod.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: nginx
```

Run:

```sh
kyverno apply policy.yaml --resource pod.yaml --audit-warn
```
and
```sh
echo $?
```

Actual output:

```text
Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
policy audit -> resource default/Pod/demo failed as audit warning:
1 -  audit failure

pass: 0, fail: 1, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0

1
```

### Expected behavior

With `--audit-warn`, an audit-only `ValidatingPolicy` violation should be counted as a warning, not a failure. In the example above, the summary should report `fail: 0, warn: 1`, and the process should exit `0`.

This should mirror the behavior for legacy `Policy` and `ClusterPolicy` resources, where audit failures are reported as warnings and do not cause `kyverno apply` to return a non-zero exit code. The current behavior makes `ValidatingPolicy` audit-only violations fail CI jobs even though they are printed as audit warnings

title: [Bug] [CLI] request.operation=CONNECT is treated as CREATE in apply/policy context
body:
## Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0 (also present on `main`)

## Description

When the CLI builds a policy context, it reads the simulated admission operation from the `request.operation` variable. The switch in `makePolicyContext` only handles `DELETE` and `UPDATE`:

https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/processor/policy_processor.go#L785-L791

`CONNECT` is a valid operation everywhere else in Kyverno (it's accepted in `request.operation` condition validation and in webhook rule operations), but here it falls through to the `Create` default set at the top of the function. So a values file or `--set request.operation=CONNECT` ends up evaluating the resource as a `CREATE` instead of a `CONNECT`.

Since the operation drives rule matching, a policy that matches only on `CONNECT` is evaluated incorrectly by the CLI compared to how it would behave in-cluster.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Write a policy whose rule matches only on the `CONNECT` operation.
2. Run `kyverno apply` against a resource with `--set request.operation=CONNECT` (or a values file setting it).
3. The rule does not match, because the CLI treats the operation as `CREATE`.

## Expected behavior

`request.operation=CONNECT` should produce a policy context with the `CONNECT` operation, matching the in-cluster behavior — the same way `UPDATE` and `DELETE` already do.

title: [Bug] [CLI] `kyverno test` incorrectly keys clone source resources by rule name only
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0

### Description

`kyverno test` incorrectly associates clone source resources when multiple generate policies contain rules with the same name.

The CLI stores and looks up clone source resources using only the rule name, assuming rule names are globally unique. However, Kyverno only requires rule names to be unique within a policy. As a result, when multiple policies share the same rule name, one entry can overwrite another, causing the wrong clone source resource to be used during test execution.

Additionally, test results are matched only by rule name, which can associate a result with the wrong policy.

This can lead to incorrect `kyverno test` results even when the policies and test configuration are valid.

1. Create two generate policies with different policy names but the same generate rule name.
2. Configure each policy to use a different `cloneSourceResource`.
3. Add both policies to a single `kyverno-test.yaml`.
4. Run:

```bash
kyverno test <test-directory>
```

One policy incorrectly uses the other policy's clone source resource, causing the test to fail.


### Expected behavior

Each policy should resolve its own clone source resource independently.

`kyverno test` should distinguish clone source resources using both the policy and the rule instead of assuming rule names are globally unique.

title: [Feature] Enable configuration to remove ANSI escape codes from text when loggingFormat=text
body:
### Problem Statement

Presently, when Kyverno emits `text` format logs, ANSI escape codes are included to colorize the output. While this is helpful when reading logs in a terminal, it makes the raw log much harder for a human to read in log aggregation tools without additional parsing. While using `json` is another option without this issue, it results in higher volume log storage. 

### Solution Description

Add another option for the `loggingFormat` [container flag](https://kyverno.io/docs/installation/customization/#container-flags) (perhaps `text-nocolor` or something) that removes ANSI escape codes.

title: [Bug] [CLI] GeneratingPolicy silently skips when resource has no metadata.uid
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.1

### Description

When using `kyverno apply` to test a `GeneratingPolicy` whose CEL expression references `object.metadata.uid` (e.g., to populate `ownerReferences`), kyverno silently produces no output if the target resource has no `uid` field. There is no error, no warning — just `pass: 0, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0`.

This is a particularly insidious failure mode in CLI-based unit tests: all-zero counts are indistinguishable from "policy correctly did not match", so the policy appears to work while generating nothing.


### Expected behavior

When a CEL expression accesses `object.metadata.uid` and the field is absent, kyverno should either:
- Report an **error** (preferred — the expression failed to evaluate), or
- Report a **skip** with a human-readable reason explaining why the rule did not fire.


### Steps to reproduce

### Steps to reproduce

**Policy:**
```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: example
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ["example.io"]
        apiVersions: ["v1alpha1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["myresources"]
  generate:
    - expression: >
        generator.Apply(object.metadata.namespace, [{
          "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
          "kind": dyn("ConfigMap"),
          "metadata": dyn({
            "name": dyn(object.metadata.name + "-generated"),
            "ownerReferences": dyn([dyn({
              "uid": dyn(object.metadata.uid)
            })])
          })
        }])
```

**Resource without uid:**
```yaml
apiVersion: example.io/v1alpha1
kind: MyResource
metadata:
  name: my-resource
  namespace: default
  # no uid field
```

```bash
kyverno apply generating-usage.yaml --resource resource-no-uid.yaml --crd-path myresource.crd.yaml
# Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
# pass: 0, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0   ← silent skip, no output
```

**Resource with uid:**
```yaml
apiVersion: example.io/v1alpha1
kind: MyResource
metadata:
  name: my-resource
  namespace: default
  uid: "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"
```

```bash
kyverno apply generating-usage.yaml --resource resource-with-uid.yaml --crd-path myresource.crd.yaml
# Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
# Generate:
# Generation completed successfully.
# pass: 1, fail: 0, warn: 0, error: 0, skip: 0   ← works as expected
```


### Expected behavior


### Why this matters

In a real cluster, every resource gets a `uid` assigned by the API server at creation time, so this bug is invisible in production. It only manifests in CLI-based unit tests where test fixtures are hand-authored and typically omit `uid`. The result is a policy that appears to pass testing while generating nothing, giving false confidence.

### Environment

- Kyverno CLI version: `1.18.1`
- Policy API: `policies.kyverno.io/v1`, `kind: GeneratingPolicy`

### Workaround

Either add a `uid` to test fixtures manually, or guard the expression against a missing field:

```cel
has(object.metadata.uid) ? dyn(object.metadata.uid) : dyn("")
```

title: [Bug] [CLI] `kyverno test` for mutating policy testing for incorrect mutation fails
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.18.0

### Description

We have several tests for (legacy) mutating policies that explicitly cover _negative_ examples of the applied mutation using `patchedResources`. That is, the patched resource intentionally differs from the result of the mutation, so we protect against undesired changes in the mutation (e.g. unintentionally changing the ordering of something).

We achieve this by setting the expected test result to `fail`.

With kyverno CLI 1.17, this works fine, but with 1.18, with changes introduced in #15361, these test cases now have a failed state and cause the test suite to fail altogether.

### Steps to reproduce

Assuming the following resources all in the same current working directory:
### `policy.yaml`
```yaml
---
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-mutation
spec:
  rules:
    - name: add-annotation
      match:
        all:
          - resources:
              kinds:
                - ConfigMap
      mutate:
        patchStrategicMerge:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              test-annotation: "foo"
```

### `resources.yaml`
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: expected-pass
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: expected-fail
```

### `results.yaml`
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: expected-pass
  annotations:
    test-annotation: foo
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: expected-fail
  annotations:
    test-annotation: bar
```

### `kyverno-test.yaml`:
```yaml
---
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: test-mutation
policies:
  - ./policy.yaml
resources:
  - resources.yaml
results:
  - policy: test-mutation
    rule: add-annotation
    patchedResources: results.yaml
    kind: ConfigMap
    resources:
      - expected-pass
    result: pass

  - policy: test-mutation
    rule: add-annotation
    patchedResources: results.yaml
    kind: ConfigMap
    resources:
      - expected-fail
    result: fail
```

Note the `result: fail` expectation in the second test case.

There, run `kyverno test --detailed-results --require-tests=true .`. Observe the following output and exit code 1:

title: [Bug] [CLI] Fails offline for CEL/ValidatingPolicy when resources include CRDs
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.17.1

### Description

We run `kyverno apply` in offline mode against rendered manifests (YAML file) as part of a CI linter. This worked reliably with classic Kyverno policies, but after migrating policies to CEL-based ValidatingPolicy, the CLI now fails whenever the input manifests include Custom Resources (e.g., External Secrets or VPA).

The failure happens even though the CR objects are present in the input file. The CLI errors out while trying to map GVK → GVR and reports “no matches for kind …”, which normally requires Kubernetes API discovery. In our CI environment we intentionally do not have cluster access, so we need an offline-friendly behavior.

This looks the same class of problem as other CLI/CEL + CRD mapping issues (for example kyverno/kyverno#15384), but in our case it happens with kyverno apply (not kyverno test).

Environment / Context
Use case: CI linter for GitOps apps (Argo CD)
Manifest source: argocd app manifests ... output saved to a file
Kyverno invocation: kyverno apply <policies> --resource <manifest.yaml> --detailed-results
No cluster access: cannot use --cluster against a real kube-apiserver
Input resources include CRDs (e.g. ExternalSecret, VerticalPodAutoscaler)

### Steps to reproduce

1. 
```
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  labels:
    argocd.argoproj.io/instance: test-staging
  name: mtest-secrets
  namespace: test
spec:
  dataFrom:
  - extract:
      key: /test
  refreshInterval: 5m
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: ssm-secret-store
  target:
    name: test-secrets
    template:
      metadata:
        annotations:
          konghq.com/basic-auth-credential: "true"
        labels:
          konghq.com/credential: basic-auth
```
2.Prepare a CEL-based Kyverno policy set (ValidatingPolicy) that is applied using kyverno apply (directory or file).

```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-requests-limits
  annotations:
    policies.kyverno.io/title: Require Limits and Requests
    policies.kyverno.io/category: Best Practices
    policies.kyverno.io/description: >-
      As application workloads share cluster resources, it is important to limit resources
      requested and consumed by each pod. It is recommended to require 'resources.requests'
      and 'resources.limits.memory' per pod. If a namespace level request or limit is specified,
      defaults will automatically be applied to each pod based on the 'LimitRange' configuration.
spec:
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  validationActions:
    - Deny
  autogen:
    podControllers:
      controllers:
        - deployments
        - daemonsets
        - statefulsets
        - cronjobs
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['']
        apiVersions: ['v1']
        operations: [CREATE, UPDATE]
        resources: ['pods']
  variables:
    - name: containers
      expression: >-
        object.spec.containers
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        variables.containers.all(c,
          has(c.resources) && has(c.resources.requests) &&
          has(c.resources.requests.memory) && c.resources.requests.memory != '' &&
          has(c.resources.requests.cpu) && c.resources.requests.cpu != '' &&
          has(c.resources.limits) && has(c.resources.limits.memory) && c.resources.limits.memory != ''
        )
      message: "CPU and memory resource requests and limits are required."
```

3. In our real setup, this came from migrating legacy ClusterPolicy rules to CEL/ValidatingPolicy.
Run kyverno apply offline against the manifest file:
`kyverno apply ./policies --resource=helm-manifest.yaml --detailed-results`

4. Output:
```
╰─ kyverno apply ./policies/require-requests-limits.yaml --resource=helm-manifest.yaml --detailed-results                                                                                                                ─╯

Applying 1 policy rule(s) to 1 resource(s)...
Error: failed to apply policies on resource mtest-secrets (failed to map gvk to gvr external-secrets.io/v1, Kind=ExternalSecret (no matches for kind "ExternalSecret" in version "external-secrets.io/v1")
)
```

### Expected behavior

In offline mode (resources loaded from local YAML), we expect one of the following:

- Kyverno CLI can evaluate CEL/ValidatingPolicy policies without requiring Kubernetes API discovery for CRDs, or
- Kyverno CLI provides a way to supply CRD information locally (e.g., `--crd-dir`, `--openapi,` or similar) so    GVK→GVR mapping works offline, or
- At minimum, Kyverno CLI should not hard-fail on GVK→GVR mapping when the resource is already fully provided as YAML input (unless the policy explicitly requires live API lookups).

Please advise if:

- offline CRD mapping for kyverno apply is expected to work for CEL/ValidatingPolicy,
- there is an existing flag or recommended pattern to provide CRD discovery offline,
- or this is a known limitation/bug to be addressed.

Why this matters
Many CI pipelines lint rendered manifests without cluster access (for security/isolation). Migrating to CEL-based ValidatingPolicy is recommended, but currently this breaks offline linting when apps contain CRDs.

title: [Bug] [CLI] GeneratingPolicy test fails with custom CRDs (GetRESTMapper ignores CRD-aware discovery for fake clients)
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.17.1

### Description

When running Kyverno test for a GeneratingPolicy that matches custom CRD resources, the CLI fails with:

```
failed to map gvk to gvr storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1, Kind=StorageBucket
(no matches for kind "StorageBucket" in version "storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1")
```
Even when CRDs are provided via ClusterResource.spec.crds (introduced in v1.17.1 via #15194), the error persists.

#### Root cause
[pkg/utils/restmapper/restmapper.go#GetRESTMapper](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/pkg/utils/restmapper/restmapper.go) detects `*kubefake.Clientset` and unconditionally falls back to a static mapper built from `data.APIGroupResources()` (built-in k8s types only). It never consults the CRD-aware `FakeDiscoveryClient` that [ext/cluster/fake.go#DClient](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/ext/cluster/fake.go) sets up with `AddGVRToGVKMapping`.

```
// restmapper.go — the fake-client branch ignores CRDs entirely
if client != nil && !isFake {
    dc := client.GetKubeClient().Discovery()
    cachedDiscovery := memory.NewMemCacheClient(dc)
    restMapper = restmapper.NewDeferredDiscoveryRESTMapper(cachedDiscovery)
} else {
    // ← always lands here for kyverno test
    apiGroupResources, err := data.APIGroupResources()
    restMapper = restmapper.NewDiscoveryRESTMapper(apiGroupResources)
}
```

The `GeneratingPolicy` code path in [cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go](https://github.com/kyverno/kyverno/blob/main/cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/test.go) calls `restMapper.RESTMapping(gvk)` for each input resource, which fails for any custom CRD.

ValidatingPolicy tests with custom CRDs work because they don't go through GetRESTMapper.

#### Possible fix

`GetRESTMapper` could use the `RESTMapper` built by `fakeCluster.RESTMapper(crds)` (which already includes CRDs) instead of creating a fresh static mapper. Alternatively, the `else` branch could query the dclient's discovery client rather than using static data.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `GeneratingPolicy` that matches a custom CRD (e.g. `StorageBucket`):
```
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1beta1
kind: GeneratingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-gpol
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: ['storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com']
        apiVersions: ['v1beta1']
        operations: ['CREATE']
        resources: ['storagebuckets']
  generate:
    - expression: |
        generator.Apply("default", [{
          "kind": dyn("ConfigMap"),
          "apiVersion": dyn("v1"),
          "metadata": dyn({"name": dyn("test"), "namespace": dyn("default")})
        }])
```
2. Create a CRD file (storagebucket-crd.yaml):
```
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: storagebuckets.storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com
spec:
  group: storage.cnrm.cloud.google.com
  names:
    kind: StorageBucket
    plural: storagebuckets
    singular: storagebucket
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
    - name: v1beta1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true
```
3. Create a ClusterResource file (clusterresources.yaml):
```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterResource
metadata:
  name: clusterresources
spec:
  crds:
    - storagebucket-crd.yaml
```

kind: StorageBucket
metadata:
  name: test-bucket

spec:

```

apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: test-gpol
clusterResources:
  - clusterresources.yaml
policies:

title: [Feature] kyverno test: Add support for mocking APICall (HTTP service calls) and GlobalContextEntry references in CLI test command
body:
cc. @realshuting 
## Description:
### Summary
The kyverno test CLI command currently silently skips context entries that rely on external data sources — specifically:
- APICall with service: URL (i.e., http.Get()-style calls to external services)
- GlobalContextEntry references (globalcontext.Get())
This makes it impossible to write offline CLI tests for policies that depend on these context types, which is a significant gap for benchmark suites and CI pipelines that validate generated policies using kyverno test.

### Current Behavior
When kyverno test runs in local mode (no clusterResources: specified), the CLI context loader wrapper in cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/store/contextloader.go nulls out the Kubernetes client and registry factory before passing them to the engine:
```
func (w wrapper) Load(...) error {
    if !w.store.IsApiCallAllowed() {
        client = nil        // disables APICall
    }
    ...
    return w.inner.Load(...)
}
```
In pkg/engine/factories/contextloaderfactory.go, when client is nil, the APICall loader is silently skipped with a log message at V(3):
```
} else if entry.APICall != nil {
    if client != nil {
        // loads data
    } else {
        l.logger.V(3).Info("disabled loading of APICall context entry")
        return nil, nil   // silently dropped
    }
}
```
Similarly, GlobalReference entries are skipped because gctxStore is never passed to the CLI context loader factory:
```
} else if entry.GlobalReference != nil {
    if gctx != nil {
        // loads data
    } else {
        l.logger.V(3).Info("disabled loading of GlobalContext context entry")
        return nil, nil   // silently dropped
    }
}
```
For CEL-based policies (ValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, GeneratingPolicy), the FakeContextProvider in pkg/cel/libs/fake_context.go flat-out panics:
```
func (f *FakeContextProvider) GetGlobalReference(name, projection string) (any, error) {
    panic("not implemented")
}
```
### Expected Behavior
Users should be able to provide static mock data in their kyverno-test.yaml (or a companion file) for both APICall service responses and GlobalContextEntry values, allowing kyverno test to resolve these context entries offline without any live cluster or external HTTP endpoint.


### Solution Description

1. Extend the Test YAML Spec
Add two new optional fields to the Test spec (cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/apis/v1alpha1/types.go):

```
apiVersion: cli.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: my-test
policies:
  - policy.yaml
resources:
  - resources.yaml

# NEW: mock static responses for http.Get() / APICall service entries
mockAPICallResponses:
  - urlPath: "https://my-external-service.example.com/api/check"
    response:
      statusCode: 200
      body:
        allowed: true

# NEW: mock static data for globalcontext.Get() / GlobalContextEntry references
mockGlobalContextEntries:
  - name: "my-gce-name"
    data:
      key: value
```

title: CLI test command reports pass for tests that should fail (multiple result-reporting bugs)
body:
## Description

The `kubectl-kyverno test` command has several bugs in how it evaluates and reports test results. These cause tests to incorrectly show "pass" when policies have runtime errors, and produce confusing output where the reason column contradicts the result column.

## Bugs Found

### Bug 1 (Critical): Legacy policy test results always pass when expected result is "fail"

**Location:** `cmd/cli/kubectl-kyverno/commands/test/output.go` lines 280, 298, 306, 347

The success computation for legacy (non-CEL) policy tests uses:
```go
success := ok || (!ok && test.Result == openreports.StatusFail)
```

This is logically equivalent to `success = ok || (test.Result == "fail")`, meaning **any test with an expected result of "fail" will always be marked as passing**, regardless of the actual engine result. For example:
- Test expects "fail", engine returns "pass" → test shows **Pass** (wrong)
- Test expects "fail", engine returns "error" → test shows **Pass** (wrong)

This produces the confusing output where the result column shows "Pass" but the reason column shows "Want fail, got pass" — the messaging inconsistency.

Note: CEL-based policy tests (ValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy, DeletingPolicy) correctly pass `ok` directly and are **not** affected by this bug.

### Bug 2: Wrong error variable in ValidatingPolicy engine response

**Location:** `pkg/cel/policies/vpol/engine/engine.go` line 198

```go
if result.Error != nil {
    response.Rules = append(response.Rules, *engineapi.RuleError(ruleName, engineapi.Validation, "error", err, nil))
```

When `result.Error` is not nil, the code passes `err` instead of `result.Error` to `RuleError`. At this point in the code, `err` is from the outer scope `Evaluate()` call which is guaranteed to be `nil` (we're in the else branch where `err == nil`). This means:
- The actual error details from `result.Error` are completely lost
- The response message is just `"error"` with no useful diagnostic information

### Bug 3: Same wrong error variable in ImageValidatingPolicy engine

**Location:** `pkg/cel/policies/ivpol/engine/engine.go` line 272

Identical issue to Bug 2:
```go
if result.Error != nil {
    response.Result = *engineapi.RuleError(ruleName, engineapi.ImageVerify, "error", err, nil)
```

`err` is nil here; should be `result.Error`.

## Impact

- **Security concern**: Broken policies with runtime errors may silently appear to pass all tests, giving false confidence
- **Testing reliability**: Test suites cannot catch policy regressions in legacy policies when expected result is "fail"
- **Debugging difficulty**: Error details are lost in CEL policy evaluation, making it hard to diagnose policy issues

## Expected Behavior

1. Test results should accurately reflect whether the expected result matches the actual result
2. Error details from `result.Error` should be included in engine responses

## Steps to Reproduce

For Bug 1, create any legacy policy test with `result: fail` in `kyverno-test.yaml`. Even if the policy has a bug causing it to return "pass" or "error", the test will still show as passing.

## Related Issues

- #15350 — messageExpression error handling (separate issue, intentionally informational per Kyverno team)
- #15351 — Missing `isValidatingPolicy: true` causes tests to fall into Bug 1's legacy code path

## Environment
- Kyverno version: main branch (commit bda351372)

title: [Feature] Unified CLI
body:
### Problem Statement

Currently, the Kyverno ecosystem uses fragmented tooling for testing different types of policies. This creates a disjointed user experience and complicates CI/CD integration for users leveraging multiple Kyverno components.

Current State:
- Core Kyverno CLI (kyverno): Supports testing for standard Kubernetes policies (ClusterPolicy, Policy) and CEL-based policies types.
- Kyverno Authz Server: Requires separate tooling or manual workflows to test HTTP and Envoy authorization policies.



### Solution Description

title: kyverno test CLI silently skips MutatingPolicy with mutateExisting: true
body:
## Description

The `kyverno test` CLI command silently skips `MutatingPolicy` resources that have `mutateExisting: true` enabled. No error or warning is produced — the policy is simply never evaluated, and the test passes vacuously.

## Root Cause

The `PolicyProcessor` calls `eng.Handle()` to process MutatingPolicies, which internally calls `provider.Fetch(ctx, false)`. The `Fetch` method filters policies based on the `mutateExisting` flag — `Fetch(ctx, false)` only returns admission-time policies, excluding any with `mutateExisting: true`.

The `Evaluate()` method (which calls `Fetch(ctx, true)`) is what processes mutateExisting policies, but only the background controller (`pkg/background/mpol/processor.go`) uses it. The CLI test tool has no equivalent path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a `MutatingPolicy` with `evaluation.mutateExisting.enabled: true`
2. Create a trigger resource, target resource, and expected patched target
3. Write a `kyverno-test.yaml` referencing all of the above with `targetResources`
4. Run `kyverno test` on the test directory

**Expected:** The target resource is mutated and the test validates the patched result.
**Actual:** The test produces no output for the mutateExisting policy. If a result is expected, it reports the resource as not found rather than showing a failure.

## Impact

Users cannot test `mutateExisting` MutatingPolicies offline before deploying them. The legacy `ClusterPolicy` mutate-existing path works correctly via `ApplyBackgroundChecks()`, but the newer CEL-based `MutatingPolicy` equivalent has no CLI test support.

title: [Bug] make codegen-helm-docs doesn't work in devcontainer
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.17.0

### Description

The `make codegen-helm-docs` Makefile target fails to find any charts when running in the devcontainer because it uses Docker volume mounts with `${PWD}`.

**Problem:**

The devcontainer is configured with `docker-outside-of-docker`, which means the Docker daemon runs on the host, not inside the devcontainer. When the Makefile runs:

```bash
docker run -v ${PWD}/charts:/work -w /work jnorwood/helm-docs:v1.14.2 -s file
```

The `${PWD}` path (e.g., `/workspaces/kyverno`) doesn't exist on the host. The host has a different path (e.g., `/home/user/workspace/kyverno`) that is mounted into the devcontainer as `/workspaces/kyverno`.

**Result:**

```console
$ make codegen-helm-docs
Generate helm docs...
time="2026-01-08T06:33:50Z" level=info msg="Found Chart directories []"
```

**Additional issue:**

The docker command also lacks the `--rm` flag, so containers accumulate over time:

```/dev/null/docker-ps.txt#L1-5
$ docker ps -a --filter "ancestor=jnorwood/helm-docs:v1.14.2"
CONTAINER ID   NAMES                STATUS
6c55529e2a7c   nifty_feynman        Exited (0) 47 seconds ago
0264a2b97f70   fervent_mendel       Exited (0) 2 days ago
...
```

**Proposed fix:**

Use the locally installed `helm-docs` binary instead of Docker. The Makefile already has a mechanism to install `helm-docs` locally via `go install`. This is similar to other tools in the Makefile.

I tried it locally and run into one additional issue. See https://github.com/norwoodj/helm-docs/issues/306.
If we add the ldflags to the go install command it works properly:

```Makefile
$(HELM_DOCS):
	@echo Install helm-docs... >&2
	@GOBIN=$(TOOLS_DIR) go install -ldflags "-X main.version=$(HELM_DOCS_VERSION:v%=%)" github.com/norwoodj/helm-docs/cmd/helm-docs@$(HELM_DOCS_VERSION)
```

This fix:
- Resolves the docker-outside-of-docker path issue
- Eliminates container cleanup issues
- Uses the existing tool installation mechanism
- Works consistently in CI, local, and devcontainer environments

title: [Bug] [CLI] kyverno test panics with mutateExisting policy using wildcard targets (name: "*")
body:
### Kyverno CLI Version

1.15.1

### Description

I have a ClusterPolicy with two rules; one is a mutating rule and the other one validates.

When testing _ONLY_ the validation rule and the mutating rule is present within the same ClusterPolicy, the kyverno CLI exist with a panic error:
```
panic: coding error: you must register resource to list kind for every resource you're going to LIST when creating the client.  See NewSimpleDynamicClientWithCustomListKinds or register the list into the scheme: /v1, Resource=namespaces out of map[]
```

Testing if the ClusterPolicy has ONLY the mutation rule succeeds.
Testing if the ClusterPolicy has ONLY the validation rule succeeds.

The panic is caused only if both rules exist within the same ClusterPolicy and I am testing only for the validation rule.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create the policy with 2 rules:
  ```yaml
  apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
  kind: ClusterPolicy
  metadata:
    name: warn-context-ns-label
  spec:
    rules:
      - name: add-context-ns-label
        match:
          all:
            - resources:
                kinds:
                  - Namespace
        mutate:
          patchStrategicMerge:
            metadata:
              labels:
                context: "error"
          mutateExistingOnPolicyUpdate: true
          targets:
            - apiVersion: v1
              kind: Namespace
              name: "*"
      - name: warn-on-invalid-or-missing-context-ns-label
         match:
           all:
             - resources:
                kinds:
                  - Namespace
          validate:
            message: "The `context` label is either missing or has an invalid value. Please check your configurations."
            allowExistingViolations: false
            failureAction: Audit
            pattern:
              metadata:
                labels:
                  context: "app|infra|lab"
```
2. Create a `kyverno-test.yaml`:
    ```yaml

    kind: Test
    metadata:
      name: test-warn-context-label
    policies:
      - ../../policies/label-enforcement/this-is-a-test.yaml
    resources:
      - default-namespace.yaml
    results:
      - policy: warn-context-ns-label
         rule: warn-on-invalid-or-missing-context-ns-label
         isMutatingPolicy: false
         resources:
           - default
         kind: Namespace

    ```

### Expected behavior

When running `kyverno test` on a policy containing `mutateExisting` with wildcard targets (`name: "*"`), the CLI should handle the test execution without panicking.

I understand that the Kyverno CLI evaluates _all_ rules in a policy during testing, and I'm not necessarily requesting the ability to test individual rules in isolation. However, the current panic error should not occur.

title: [Bug] ImageValidatingPolicy does not enforce validations for pods/ephemeralcontainers subresource requests
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

GKE

### Kyverno Rule Type

ImageValidatingPolicy

### Description

When an `ImageValidatingPolicy` includes `pods/ephemeralcontainers` in its `matchConstraints.resourceRules`, the webhook is correctly registered and fires for subresource requests (e.g. `kubectl debug`). The mutating webhook handler resolves images and runs `verifyImageSignatures` (visible in logs). However, the validating webhook handler never evaluates the `validations` expression, so unsigned ephemeral containers are always admitted.

A `ValidatingPolicy` targeting the same subresource with `expression: "false"` correctly denies the request, confirming the Kubernetes API server does deliver the admission review. The bug is in the IVPOL validating handler specifically.


## Additional Context

To confirm the API server is delivering the admission review for `pods/ephemeralcontainers`, I applied a `ValidatingPolicy` (not ImageValidatingPolicy) targeting the same subresource:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-block-ephemeral
spec:
  validationActions: [Deny]
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods/ephemeralcontainers"]
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        enforce-signing: "true"
  validations:
    - expression: "false"
      message: "blocked"
```

This correctly denied the `kubectl debug` request, proving the webhook fires and the API server delivers the review. The issue is isolated to the IVPOL handler not evaluating validations for subresource requests.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Kyverno 1.18.2
2. Create a namespace with a label for the policy selector:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: ephemeral-container-test
  labels:
    enforce-signing: "true"
```

3. Apply this ImageValidatingPolicy:

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: verify-image-ephemeral
spec:
  webhookConfiguration:
    timeoutSeconds: 30
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: false
  validationActions: [Deny]
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods", "pods/ephemeralcontainers"]
    namespaceSelector:
      matchLabels:
        enforce-signing: "true"
  matchImageReferences:
    - glob: "*"
  credentials:
    providers:
      - google
  attestors:
    - name: cosign
      cosign:
        key:
          data: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            <your-public-key>
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
        ctlog:
          url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev
          insecureIgnoreTlog: true
          insecureIgnoreSCT: true
  variables:
    - name: allImages
      expression: >-
        images.?containers.orValue([])
        + images.?initContainers.orValue([])
        + images.?ephemeralContainers.orValue([])
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        variables.allImages.map(image,
          verifyImageSignatures(image, [attestors.cosign])
        ).all(e, e > 0)
      message: All container images must be signed.
```

4. Create a pod with a signed image:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: signed-pod
  namespace: ephemeral-container-test
spec:
  containers:
    - name: nginx
      image: gcr.io/my-project/nginx@sha256:<signed-digest>
```

5. Attach an unsigned debug container:

```sh
kubectl debug signed-pod -n ephemeral-container-test \
  --image=busybox:latest --target=nginx
```


### Expected behavior

The debug container should be denied:

```
Error from server: admission webhook "ivpol.validate.kyverno.svc-..." denied the request:
Policy verify-image-ephemeral failed: All container images must be signed.
```

## Actual Behaviour

The debug container is admitted without error. The admission controller logs show the mutating webhook *did* attempt image verification and correctly found no signatures:

```
ERR image verification failed error="failed to verify cosign signatures: no signatures found"
    attestor=cosign image=busybox:latest
```

But the validating webhook handler does not evaluate the `validations` expression for the subresource request.

### Screenshots

_No response_

```Shell

```

title: [Bug] ImageValidatingPolicy verification fails for single-arch (arm64-only) image indexes: "no child with platform linux/amd64 in index"
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.33.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

`ImageValidatingPolicy` image signature verification fails for images published as a
single-architecture **arm64-only** OCI index. Kyverno defaults to resolving `linux/amd64`,
which isn't present in the index, so evaluation errors out before signatures are ever
checked.

**Admission error:**

    FailedCreate  Error creating: admission webhook "ivpol.validate.kyverno.svc-fail"
    denied the request: Policy <policy-name> error: failed to evaluate policy:
    no child with platform linux/amd64 in index <registry>/<repo>:<arm64-only-tag>

Related: same root cause as #13591 (which tracks the legacy `imageRegistry` path); no
existing issue covers the `ImageValidatingPolicy` (new API) path.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the sample [verify-image-ivpol](https://kyverno.io/policies/other/verify-image-ivpol/verify-image-ivpol/) policy and click "Open in Playground".
2. In the Playground, change `matchImageReferences` to:

   ```yaml
   matchImageReferences:
     - glob: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/gitlab-runner-helper:*
   ```
3. Add the Pod below (an image built exclusively for arm64).

4. Click "Start".

5. The Pod errors with `no child with platform linux/amd64 in index` .

Pod:

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: arm
spec:
  containers:
    - image: registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/gitlab-runner-helper:arm64-v18.1.0
      name: helper-arm
```

### Expected behavior

Kyverno should verify arm64-only images successfully, instead of always looking for a
`linux/amd64` variant and failing when it isn't there.

Two possible fixes (not mutually exclusive):

- **Auto-pick when unambiguous:** if the image is built for only one architecture, Kyverno
  should just use that one instead of insisting on `linux/amd64`.
- **Let the policy choose:** add an optional `platform` field to `ImageValidatingPolicy`
  so the author can say which architecture to verify (e.g. `linux/arm64`). This is the
  same approach already approved in PR #13635 for the older policy type.

title: [Bug] ClusterPolicy verifyImages ignores --registryCredentialHelpers when the pod has imagePullSecrets
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Description

### Description

A `kyverno.io/v1` ClusterPolicy `verifyImages` rule stops using the `--registryCredentialHelpers` keychains as soon as the admitted pod has `imagePullSecrets`, unless the rule also sets `imageRegistryCredentials.providers`. The registry client ends up with no credential providers, so the manifest fetch goes out anonymously and verification fails:

```
.attestors[0].entries[0].keys: GET https://<account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/v2/<repo>/manifests/<tag>: unexpected status code 401 Unauthorized: Not Authorized
```

It breaks between 1.17.2 and 1.18.0. 1.17.2 is the last version I saw it work on, and it still fails on 1.18.1 and 1.18.2.

In `pkg/engine/factories/registryclientfactory.go`, 1.17.2 returns the global client whenever the policy sets no credentials of its own, so the keychains configured by the flag still apply:

```go
func (f *registryClientFactory) GetClient(ctx context.Context, creds *kyvernov1.ImageRegistryCredentials) (engineapi.RegistryClient, error) {
	if creds != nil {
		// ... per-request client ...
	}
	return f.globalClient, nil
}
```

1.18.0 added `imagePullSecrets` to that condition. Now any pod with pull secrets takes the per-request branch, where `WithCredentialProviders` is skipped because `creds` is nil:

```go
func (f *registryClientFactory) GetClient(ctx context.Context, creds *kyvernov1.ImageRegistryCredentials, resourceNamespace string, imagePullSecrets []string) (engineapi.RegistryClient, error) {
	if creds != nil || len(imagePullSecrets) > 0 {
		registryOptions := []registryclient.Option{
			registryclient.WithTracing(),
		}
		if creds != nil && len(creds.Providers) > 0 {
			registryOptions = append(registryOptions, registryclient.WithCredentialProviders(providers...))
		}
		// only WithKeychainPullSecrets is appended
		client, err := registryclient.New(registryOptions...)
```

The client is left with `WithTracing()` and the pull-secret keychain, so none of the keychains from the flag get added. I hit it with `amazon`, where it means IRSA is never used, but it applies to any of them.

`main` still does this after #16439 - the early return only helps when there are no pull secrets at all:

```go
// creds is nil. create a registry client with only the imagePullSecrets and no providers
client := registryclient.New(f.secretsLister, resourceNamespace, secretsJoined, "", false)
```

Not the same as #15776 / #16510, which cover the CEL `MutatingPolicy` `image.GetMetadata()` path and are fixed by #16439.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Cosign-sign an image into a private ECR repo using a KMS key.
2. Give the admission controller ECR access via IRSA, leave `--registryCredentialHelpers` at its default, and don't set `imageRegistryCredentials` on the policy.
3. Apply a ClusterPolicy with a `verifyImages` rule matching that image and a `keys.kms` attestor.
4. Create a pod referencing the image, where the pod or its ServiceAccount has any `imagePullSecrets`.

Verification fails with the 401 above. Removing the `imagePullSecrets`, or adding `imageRegistryCredentials.providers: [amazon]` to the rule, makes it pass. IRSA itself is fine on the failing versions: `AWS_ROLE_ARN` and `AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` are both set and the projected token is readable by the container.

### Expected behavior

`--registryCredentialHelpers` should still apply when a policy sets no `imageRegistryCredentials`. Pull secrets and the global providers should compose instead of pull secrets silently replacing them. One fix would be to seed the per-request options with the global providers when `creds` is nil.

Is this intended? If `imageRegistryCredentials.providers` is now required whenever the admitted pod has pull secrets, that seems worth documenting, since the same policy verifies or fails depending on whether the pod happens to carry a pull secret, which the policy author doesn't control.

### Slack discussion

title: [Bug] ImageValidatingPolicy requires a Rekor URL when insecureIgnoreTlog is enabled
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.34.x

### Kubernetes Platform

EKS

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

An `ImageValidatingPolicy` using Cosign public-key verification fails for Rekorless signatures when `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true` is configured without a `ctlog.url`.

Example attestor configuration:

```yaml
attestors:
  - name: privateKey
    cosign:
      key:
        data: |
          -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
          ...
          -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
      ctlog:
        insecureIgnoreTlog: true
```

The image is signed with Cosign and stored in a private registry without a Rekor entry.

When a Pod using the image is created, admission is denied with:

Policy verify-rekorless-image failed: policy not evaluated

The admission controller logs show the underlying error:

failed to build cosign verification opts: getting Rekor public keys: rekor URL must be provided

In Kyverno v1.18.2, `getRekor(ctx, att.CTLog)` is called before `opts.IgnoreTlog` is assigned in `pkg/image/verifiers/ivpol/cosign/opts.go`.

As a result, verification fails when ctlog.url is empty before insecureIgnoreTlog can take effect.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign an image with a Cosign key without uploading an entry to Rekor.
2. Configure an IVP attestor with the public key and `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog: true`.
3. Do not configure `ctlog.url`.
4. Create a Pod using the signed image.
5. Observe that admission is denied with rekor URL must be provided.

### Expected behavior

When `ctlog.insecureIgnoreTlog` is true, IVP should skip Rekor initialization and verify the signature without requiring `ctlog.url`.

The equivalent ClusterPolicy verifyImages configuration works with `rekor.ignoreTlog: true`.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```Shell
2026-07-31T05:32:52Z0m ERR0m github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/imageverification/imageverifiers/cosign/verifier.go:590m36m >0m image verification failed0m error=0m31m1m"failed to build cosign verification opts: getting Rekor public keys:  rekor URL must be provided"0m0m attestor=xxx digest=sha256:xxxxxxx image=registry.company.com/internal/image:tag logger=Cosign

title: verifyImages: cosignOCI11:true still reports no signatures found for OCI-1.1-Referrers-only images (Cilium, CloudNativePG)
body:
## Description

On Kyverno **v1.18.2** (Helm chart `kyverno/kyverno` **3.8.2**), a `ClusterPolicy` `verifyImages` rule with `cosignOCI11: true` and a correct keyless `issuer` / `subjectRegExp` still reports:

```text
.attestors[0].entries[0].keyless: no signatures found
```

for third-party images whose signatures are published **only** via the OCI 1.1 Referrers API (no legacy `sha256-<digest>.sig` tag).

This is a **signature discovery** failure, not an identity mismatch. The same image references verify successfully with the `cosign` CLI from the same host, and the Fulcio identity extracted from `cosign download signature` + `openssl x509 -text` matches the policy fields exactly.

## Reproduction

### Image A — Cilium (quay.io)

```bash
# cosign CLI succeeds
cosign verify \
  --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/cilium/cilium/.github/workflows/.*' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
  quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.19.3

# digest used in our live cluster:
# sha256:2e61680593cddca8b6c055f6d4c849d87a26a1c91c7e3b8b56c7fb76ab7b7b10
```

Kyverno rule (Audit or Enforce — same discovery error):

```yaml
verifyImages:
  - imageReferences: ["quay.io/cilium/cilium:*"]
    cosignOCI11: true
    required: true
    attestors:
      - count: 1
        entries:
          - keyless:
              issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
              subjectRegExp: "^https://github\\.com/cilium/cilium/\\.github/workflows/.*"
              rekor:
                url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev
```

Admission warning:

```text
failed to verify image quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.19.3: .attestors[0].entries[0].keyless: no signatures found
```

### Image B — CloudNativePG (ghcr.io) — same class of failure

```bash
cosign verify \
  --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg/.github/workflows/.*' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer 'https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' \
  ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg:1.30.0
# succeeds; cosign tree shows "artifacts via OCI referrer"
```

Kyverno with the matching keyless identity + `cosignOCI11: true` still reports `no signatures found`.

### Counter-examples that *do* verify under the same Kyverno build

These keyless (or static-key) images admit cleanly with no `no signatures found` warning on the same cluster/policy engine:

- `quay.io/openbao/openbao:2.2.0` (keyless, GH Actions OIDC)
- `cr.l5d.io/linkerd/controller:edge-26.7.2` (keyless)
- `quay.io/cilium/tetragon:v1.7.0` (keyless)
- `quay.io/jetstack/cert-manager-controller:v1.21.0` (static key, `signatureAlgorithm: sha512`, `rekor.ignoreTlog: true`)

So this is not a blanket keyless or network failure.

## Root-cause notes (from reading Kyverno v1.18.2 + cosign sources)

Full trace: we walked `api/kyverno/v1/image_verification_types.go` (`CosignOCI11`), `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/cosign.go` (`ExperimentalOCI11 = opts.CosignOCI11`), and cosign's `VerifyImageSignatures` (OCI 1.1 experimental path only when the flag is set; otherwise legacy signature-tag lookup). The policy field is set correctly and matches the documented code path, but in practice Kyverno still fails to discover Referrers-only signatures for the images above.

Not a network issue from the admission-controller pod: egress to `quay.io` / `ghcr.io` / `rekor.sigstore.dev` confirmed live.

## Expected

With `cosignOCI11: true`, Kyverno's verifyImages path should discover and verify the same Referrers-API signatures that `cosign verify` finds for the same reference and identity.

## Kyverno version

- Kyverno: v1.18.2
- Chart: kyverno/kyverno 3.8.2
- Cluster: Kubernetes (kubeadm), Cilium CNI

## Related

- Possibly adjacent to #16664 (bundle / referrers discovery), but that issue describes the opposite direction (signatures invisible on registries *without* referrers). This report is: **Referrers-only publishers + `cosignOCI11: true` still yield `no signatures found`.**

Happy to provide full PolicyReport / admission-controller traces if useful.

title: [IVPOL] verifyDigest and required in validationConfigurations are never enforced
body:
### Kyverno Version
main (issue written at commit 894c52c97514298a377c2411116506e7cd3214f8)

### Description

`ImageValidatingPolicy.spec.validationConfigurations` exposes `verifyDigest` and `required` (both default `true`), documented as:

- `verifyDigest`: "validates that images have a digest."
- `required`: "validates that images are verified, i.e., have passed a signature or attestation check."

Neither field is read anywhere in the CEL compiler or evaluator for `ImageValidatingPolicy`:

- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/compiler.go` (`compilerImpl.Compile`) never reads `spec.ValidationConfigurations`.
- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/policy.go` (`compiledPolicy.Evaluate`) never reads `spec.ValidationConfigurations`; it only runs `spec.Validations`/`spec.MatchImageReferences`/etc.
- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/validate.go` (`Validate`, used for policy admission-time validation) never references it either.

The only place these two fields are consulted at all is `pkg/controllers/webhook/controller.go` (`ivpolsNeedingMutation`), and only to decide whether to register a mutating webhook, not to enforce anything.

As a result, setting `verifyDigest: true` (or leaving it at its default) has no effect: a Pod referencing an image by tag only (no digest) is not rejected/flagged for missing a digest unless the policy author separately writes a CEL `validations` expression to check for it. Likewise, `required: true` has no effect: there's no check anywhere that an image was actually verified (e.g. that at least one `attestors`/`validations` check ran and passed) before being allowed through.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install an `ImageValidatingPolicy` relying only on `validationConfigurations` for enforcement, with no custom CEL validation duplicating the same check, e.g.:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1
   kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
   metadata:
     name: require-digest
   spec:
     validationActions: [Deny]
     validationConfigurations:
       verifyDigest: true
       required: true
     matchImageReferences:
       - glob: "ghcr.io/**"
     attestors:
       - name: cosign-key
         cosign:
           key:
             data: <public-key>
     validations:
       - expression: "true"
   ```
2. Create a Pod with `image: ghcr.io/example/app:latest` (tag only, no digest, and not actually verified against `cosign-key`).
3. Observe the admission result.

### Expected behavior

The request should be denied because the image has no digest (`verifyDigest: true`) and/or was not verified against any configured attestor (`required: true`).

### Actual behavior

The request is admitted. The `validations` CEL expression (`true`) is the only thing evaluated; `verifyDigest`/`required` are silently ignored.

### Relevant code

- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/compiler.go` — `compilerImpl.Compile`
- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/policy.go` — `compiledPolicy.Evaluate`
- `pkg/image/verification/evaluator/validate.go` — `Validate`
- `github.com/kyverno/api` `api/policies.kyverno.io/v1alpha1/imagevalidating_policy.go` — `ValidationConfiguration.VerifyDigest` / `.Required` field definitions

### Troubleshooting
- [x] I have read and followed the documentation and the troubleshooting guide.
- [x] I have searched other issues in this repository and mine is not recorded.

title: [Bug] verifyImages panics with nil pointer dereference when fetching sigstore bundle attestations without 'type'
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.2

### Kubernetes Version

1.31.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

When `verifyImages` is configured with `sigstoreBundle: true` to verify **attestations**, and the `attestations[].type` (or the deprecated `attestations[].predicateType`) field is left unset, the admission controller panics with a nil pointer dereference instead of returning a policy failure.

Both `Attestation.Type` and `Attestation.PredicateType` are marked `+kubebuilder:validation:Optional` in the CRD (`api/kyverno/v1/image_verification_types.go`), so omitting them is a supported configuration — e.g. when a user just wants to check that *any* attestation exists/verifies for an image without filtering by predicate type. Today that configuration crashes verification instead of working or failing gracefully.

I tracked it down to `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go`:

- `fetchBundles()` only populates `verificationBundle.DSSE_Envelope` inside the `if predicateType != ""` branch. When no `type`/`predicateType` is set, the bundles it returns have `DSSE_Envelope == nil`.
- `decodeStatementsFromBundles()` unconditionally dereferences that field: `intotostatement = *b.Bundle.DSSE_Envelope`, which panics when it's `nil`.

I reproduced the panic locally with a minimal unit test that feeds `decodeStatementsFromBundles` a `verificationResult` whose `Bundle.DSSE_Envelope` is `nil` (the exact shape returned by `fetchBundles` in this scenario):

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=...]

goroutine ...:
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign.decodeStatementsFromBundles(...)
	pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go:259
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign.(*verifier).FetchAttestations(...)
	pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/verifier.go:105
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign an image and attach an in-toto attestation using cosign's new bundle format so it's published as an OCI referrer with artifact type `application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle+json`:
   ```
   cosign attest --predicate predicate.json --new-bundle-format --yes <image>
   ```
2. Apply a ClusterPolicy that verifies attestations via `sigstoreBundle: true` **without** setting `type`/`predicateType` on the attestation entry:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
   kind: ClusterPolicy
   metadata:
     name: check-attestations
   spec:
     rules:
       - name: verify-attestations
         match:
           any:
             - resources:
                 kinds: [Pod]
         verifyImages:
           - imageReferences:
               - "ghcr.io/example/*"
             sigstoreBundle: true
             attestations:
               - attestors:
                   - entries:
                       - keyless:
                           subject: "https://github.com/example/repo/*"
                           issuer: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
   ```
3. Create a Pod referencing the attested image and watch the `kyverno-admission-controller` logs/pod status.

### Expected behavior

Kyverno should either evaluate the attestation regardless of predicate type (since `type` is documented as optional), or return a clear policy validation error telling the user that `type` is required for `sigstoreBundle` attestation checks — not crash the controller.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Kyverno logs

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x...]

goroutine 1 [running]:
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign.decodeStatementsFromBundles(...)
	pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go:259
github.com/kyverno/kyverno/pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign.(*verifier).FetchAttestations(...)
	pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/verifier.go:105
```

title: [Bug] ImageValidatingPolicy: attestation verification returns 0 for valid cosign v3 (new bundle format, OCI referrer) attestations; Deny rejects with "policy not evaluated" and a matching PolicyException cannot except
body:
**Kyverno version**: 1.18.1 (Helm chart 3.8.1). The latest release, 1.18.2, contains no image-verification changes, so we expect it to reproduce there as well; not yet re-tested in-cluster.
**Kubernetes**: v1.35 (EKS)
**Registry**: ghcr.io (pull secret provided via `credentials.secrets`)
**Cosign**: v3.0.6, default settings (no bundle-format, tlog, or referrer flags)

## Description

An `ImageValidatingPolicy` (policies.kyverno.io/v1) that requires an in-toto attestation via `verifyAttestationSignatures(...)` always returns count 0 for attestations created by cosign v3 with default settings, even though `cosign verify-attestation` verifies the exact same attestation on the same image digest with the same identity successfully (exit 0).

Cosign v3 stores attestations in the new bundle format as OCI referrers. On ghcr.io the referrer is reachable only through the fallback tag `sha256-<digest>` (ghcr's Referrers API returns an empty list), and no legacy `.att` tag is created. Kyverno's image signature verification handles this layout correctly: a sibling IVP verifying cosign v3 image signatures with the same keyless config shape, registry, and credentials enforces Deny without problems. Only the attestation path fails.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Build and push an image, then attest it with cosign v3 defaults (ours runs in GitHub Actions with keyless signing; the predicate is a SLSA Verification Summary):

```
cosign attest --yes \
  --type "https://slsa.dev/verification_summary/v1" \
  --predicate vsa.json \
  "${IMAGE}@${DIGEST}"
```

2. Confirm the attestation is valid and discoverable by cosign (this passes):

```
cosign verify-attestation \
  --type "https://slsa.dev/verification_summary/v1" \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  --certificate-identity-regexp "<producer workflow SAN regex>" \
  "${IMAGE}@${DIGEST}"
```

Storage layout at this point: the attestation exists as a new-bundle-format OCI referrer under the fallback tag `sha256-<digest>`; there is no `.att` tag; the ghcr Referrers API response is empty.

3. Apply an ImageValidatingPolicy requiring that attestation (trimmed to essentials):

```yaml
apiVersion: policies.kyverno.io/v1
kind: ImageValidatingPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-vsa
spec:
  validationActions: [Audit]   # also reproduced with [Deny]
  failurePolicy: Ignore
  webhookConfiguration:
    timeoutSeconds: 30
  evaluation:
    background:
      enabled: false
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods"]
  matchImageReferences:
    - glob: "ghcr.io/myorg/*"
  credentials:
    secrets:
      - registry-pull-secret
  attestations:
    - name: vsa
      intoto:
        type: https://slsa.dev/verification_summary/v1
  attestors:
    - name: producer
      cosign:
        keyless:
          identities:
            - issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
              subjectRegExp: <producer workflow SAN regex>
        ctlog:
          url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev
  validationConfigurations:
    mutateDigest: false
    verifyDigest: true
    required: true
  validations:
    - expression: >-
        images.containers.map(image,
          verifyAttestationSignatures(image, attestations.vsa, [attestors.producer])).all(e, e > 0)
      message: image must carry a verified VSA
```

4. Create a pod using the attested image (referenced by digest).

## Expected behavior

`verifyAttestationSignatures` returns >= 1 (the attestation exists, is bound to the digest, is signed by the matching identity, and cosign verifies it), so the CEL expression passes and the admission result is pass.

## Actual behavior

- `verifyAttestationSignatures` evaluates to 0 for every attested image, so the expression fails.
- In Audit, the metric records a genuine policy failure, not an error: `kyverno_image_validating_policy_execution_duration_seconds_count{policy_name="require-vsa", result="fail"}` increments while `result="error"` stays 0.
- In Deny, the pod is rejected, and the deny message is `policy not evaluated` instead of the policy's own `message`.
- The pod annotation `kyverno.io/imageverify-outcomes` contains no entry at all for this policy on affected admissions.
- `failurePolicy: Ignore` does not help, consistent with the failure being returned as a valid deny response rather than a webhook error.
- A `PolicyException` (policies.kyverno.io/v1) targeting this policy, with a CEL matchCondition allowlisting specific digests and `reportResult: skip`, works as expected in Audit (skips are recorded) but does NOT except under Deny: pods on excepted digests are denied identically, with the same `policy not evaluated`. Even the exception path produces the same opaque outcome, so the defect may sit in the outcome handling for this policy type rather than only in attestation fetching.

## Impact

Any IVP gating on attestations is un-enforceable for images attested with current cosign defaults: flipping to Deny blocks every properly attested image, and because the PolicyException fails the same way, every allowlisted one too. In our case this denied re-admission of production workloads fleet-wide until we reverted the policy to Audit.

## Additional context

- Debugging is compounded by #16023: the IVP CEL path produces no logs even at `-v=6`, so there is no server-side trace of why the count is 0.
- Signature verification with the same keyless/ctlog configuration, registry, and credentials works correctly in a sibling IVP, isolating the problem to the attestation path (`attestations.intoto` plus `verifyAttestationSignatures`).
- Not yet tested: whether re-attesting in the legacy storage layout (`.att` tag) makes the same policy pass, and v1.18.2 in-cluster (its release notes and commits contain no image-verification changes).

title: verifyImages: cosign 3.x bundle signatures invisible on registries without OCI referrers API (fallback-tag descriptors typed oci.empty are filtered out)
body:
## Summary

On registries that do **not** implement the OCI 1.1 referrers API (e.g. GHCR, which returns `404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN` for `/v2/<repo>/referrers/<digest>`), Kyverno 1.18.2's cosign verifier reports **"no signatures found"** for images that *do* have valid cosign 3.x bundle signatures. `cosign verify` on the same image succeeds.

## Root cause (verified end-to-end)

1. `fetchBundles` in `pkg/image/verifiers/cpol/cosign/sigstore.go` calls `remote.Referrers(subject)`. The registry has no referrers API, so go-containerregistry falls back to the **fallback tag scheme**: it reads the tag `sha256-<subject-digest>` as an OCI index.
2. Cosign 3.x writes that fallback-tag index with member descriptors typed **`application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json`** (the real artifactType only exists on the referenced manifests themselves).
3. `fetchBundles` then filters descriptors with:
   ```go
   if !strings.HasPrefix(manifestDesc.ArtifactType, "application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle") {
       continue
   }
   ```
   (sigstore.go:~105, release-1.18)
   Every descriptor from the fallback index is skipped → zero bundles → "no signatures found".
4. cosign's own verifier ignores the descriptor-level artifactType and parses the referenced manifests, which is why CLI verification passes and masks the problem.

So on any registry without a referrers API, the combination *cosign ≥3.x (bundle format) + Kyverno 1.18* can never verify, regardless of credentials.

## Reproduction

```bash
# sign any image with cosign 3.x (new bundle format is the default)
cosign sign --yes ghcr.io/<org>/<image>@sha256:<digest>
# confirm discovery only works via the fallback tag:
curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json" \
  https://ghcr.io/v2/<org>/<image>/referrers/sha256:<digest>   # 404 MANIFEST_UNKNOWN
curl -H "Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json" \
  https://ghcr.io/v2/<org>/<image>/manifests/sha256-<digest>   # 200, but members typed application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json
```

Then a standard verifyImages policy:

```yaml
verifyImages:
- imageReferences: ["ghcr.io/<org>/*"]
  imageRegistryCredentials:
    secrets: [kyverno/registry-creds]
  attestors:
  - entries:
    - keyless:
        issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
        subjectRegExp: https://github.com/<org>/<repo>/.*
        rekor: {url: https://rekor.sigstore.dev}
```

admission is denied with `no signatures found` / `no matching attestations`.

## Expected behavior

When the descriptor artifactType is empty/unknown (fallback-tag path), the verifier should fetch the referenced manifest and inspect its actual `artifactType` (or the bundle layer mediaType) before discarding it — i.e. the filter should not rely solely on the descriptor in the index.

## Environment

- Kyverno 1.18.2 (helm chart 3.8.2), admission controller only
- Registry: GHCR (ghcr.io), private packages
- Signer: cosign v3.1.0 (sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 in GitHub Actions)
- Verified the PAT/auth path is fine: with `imageRegistryCredentials` the token exchange succeeds and the *signature fetch* is where discovery dies.

## Workaround we are shipping

After signing, we rewrite the fallback-tag index with the real per-manifest artifactTypes (via `oras manifest fetch`/`push`), which makes Kyverno 1.18.2 discover the bundles. Happy to contribute the fix upstream if you can point at the preferred approach (manifest fetch on unknown descriptor type vs. dropping the prefix filter).

title: Add bounded verification cache support to ImageValidatingPolicy
body:
### Problem Statement

Kyverno's classic `ClusterPolicy` / `Policy` `verifyImages` path supports bounded successful-verification reuse through `useCache` and the admission controller's `--imageVerifyCacheEnabled`, `--imageVerifyCacheMaxSize`, and `--imageVerifyCacheTTLDuration` settings.

The typed `ImageValidatingPolicy` path does not use that cache and exposes no equivalent setting. In current `main` (`b26c1d8c964e20dc4041b8c725f2ca1a008b4f99`), `pkg/cel/policies/ivpol/engine/engine.go` creates a fresh SDK `ImageContext` for each mutating admission request. The shared `ImageVerifyCacheClient` is passed only to the classic engine, where `pkg/engine/internal/imageverifier.go` calls `Get` and `Set` around successful verification.

As a result, repeated admissions of the same digest under an unchanged typed policy repeatedly fetch and verify the same registry signature. A burst of concurrent Pod admissions therefore amplifies registry traffic, credential use, signature parsing, and webhook latency even when every request references the same already-verified digest. This matters most in fail-closed installations, where registry latency or controller saturation can convert redundant work into admission timeouts.

### Solution Description

Provide supported, bounded successful-verification reuse for `ImageValidatingPolicy` and `NamespacedImageValidatingPolicy`, with behavior equivalent in security posture to the classic verifier cache.

At minimum, the cache contract should:

- remain opt-in at the policy level and bounded by the existing global size and TTL controls;
- key successful results by immutable image digest plus the complete policy identity and resource version, so policy, attestor, key, credential, or validation changes invalidate prior results;
- cache successes only, never registry/authentication failures or failed verification;
- work for both clustered and namespaced typed policies;
- expose hit/miss/eviction metrics so operators can verify that reuse is active;
- preserve fail-closed behavior on cache miss or cache failure.

Reusing the existing `ImageVerifyCacheClient` would keep one controller-level cache implementation if its key and result granularity are sufficient. If typed CEL verification needs a more granular result, the implementation should still share the same bounded lifecycle and invalidation semantics rather than introduce an unbounded second cache.

### Alternatives

- **Use classic `ClusterPolicy.verifyImages`:** this restores native `useCache` today but requires leaving the typed policy API solely for an implementation-path limitation.
- **Serialize admissions or retry CI jobs:** this hides the redundant work and reduces throughput; it does not address the missing reuse.
- **Increase webhook timeout or registry capacity:** this makes each burst more expensive and does not remove repeated verification.
- **Rely only on the SDK request-local image map:** that map is created per admission and cannot reuse a successful result across requests.

### Additional Context

The source gap is present in both Kyverno v1.18.2 and current `main`. I found no existing issue or pull request for typed image-verification cache support after searching for `ImageValidatingPolicy cache`, `IVP useCache`, and `imageVerifyCache ImageValidatingPolicy`.

This request is independent of the separate SDK image-context concurrency defect tracked in kyverno/sdk#123. Fixing that race makes request-local loading safe; it does not provide cross-request verification reuse.

title: Vulnerability detected: CVE-2026-49834 (medium)
body:
### Impact
_What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_

A verifier configured with WithTransparencyLog(N>1) or WithSignedCertificateTimestamps(N>1) expected defense-in-depth against the compromise of a single log instance. However, threshold counting counted verified witnesses per-entry or per-validation-path rather than per-log-authority.

As a result, a single compromised transparency log could forge multiple entries with different indices, and a single compromised CT log could verify multiple times (either across multiple certificate chains or via multiple embedded SCTs), fully satisfying the multi-log threshold requirements and defeating the multi-log policy.

Note that this does not affect Cosign, as Cosign sets a threshold of 1.

### Patches
_Has the problem been patched? What versions should users upgrade to?_

Upgrade to v1.1.5.

### Workarounds
_Is there a way for users to fix or remediate the vulnerability without upgrading?_

There is no workaround, beyond relying on trusted logs.

---

**Affected branches:**

title: [Bug] Cosign key based verification panics unless you explicitly set the transparency log verify to false
body:
### Kyverno Version

1.18.0

### Kubernetes Version

1.35.x

### Kubernetes Platform

KinD

### Kyverno Rule Type

verifyImages

### Description

In kyverno image verify, if you use a policy with a cosign attestor and don't explicitly specify that the ctlog verification should be skipped, the admission controller panics
